Name: Elena Gold
Question: How are Ukrainians coping with the constant bombardments in their cities?
Answer: “I'm fine :)” installation made of Ukrainian road signs riddled with shrapnel and bullet holes at the "Burning Man" festival in the Black Rock Desert in Nevada is such a perfect expression of how Ukrainians feel. (Video in the comments below.) Usually people in Ukraine answer "Fine" to the question "How are you?" But every Ukrainian had lost friends, family members, neighbors or colleagues to this war. Every Ukrainian personally knows someone who is now at the front line, defending the country with weapons in his or her hands. 2 heroes. At the 2024 Paris Paralympics, Ukraine has the largest delegation in its history. You don’t need to guess why. The residents of small Ukrainian towns and villages located near the border with Russia are hit the hardest. They went to bed at home, and in the morning they lost everything — lucky to have survived at all. For 2.5 years, Ukrainians don’t let Russia to break their spirits. When Ukrainians answer, 'I'm fine', they mean that they continue being resilient, continue staying strong, continue choosing to be fine. Class of 2022 graduate in her prom dress on the rubble of her Kharkiv school, destroyed by the Russian artillery. “Each Ukrainian living now is a winner. The one whose family survived and got through the horrible past of occupations, genocides and wars,” writes Anton Geraschenko, former advisor to the minister of internal affairs of Ukraine. “We know what it's like to fight for our existence. We know what it’s like to protect our land. We fight and we stand now. We know how to survive, and now we will win this battle,” asserts Gerashchenko. Yana Zalevskai is a 23-year-old soldier of the 59th Brigade. She was 13 in 2014, when Russia invaded Crimea and Donbas. Yana is from Kherson. During the Russian occupation of the city in 2022, she attended anti-Russian rallies. After the city was de-occupied by the Ukrainian army, she decided to join the defenders — first as a combat medic, and then she learned to be a drone operator. Yana's father is also a soldier and has been fighting Russians in Donbas since 2014. Yana’s mother and daughter are waiting for her return at home. Yana was injured in early August and is now recovering. "I really want to end this war. I don't want our children to go to war,” says Yana. Ukrainians are resilient because they have to outlast Russia in this war. Because otherwise, there will be no Ukraine. Because they don’t want to leave this war to their kids. War and genocide must become something not to live through, but a thing from history books. The Ukrainian children should be able to grow up in peace and safety. That’s what drives Ukrainians to keep going, no matter what.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What is the future of Russia? With an authoritarian government lead by Vladimir Putin, who now has troops fighting in Ukraine and potentially Syria, is Russia's future doomed?
Answer: 62-year-old Aleksandr Dugin (centre) is the main ideologist behind Vladimir Putin’s regime. That’s the picture of the future of Russia — women in black headscarves, men with beards, huts in the woods. Dugin is a “Christian orthodox philosopher”, an avid promoter of the “Russian world”. Name: Elena Gold
Question: What is "Russian world" ideology, which the Ukrainian government has recently banned the use of religious organisations to promote?
Answer: Priests of the “Russian world” in Severodonetsk, Ukraine. The Ukrainian town of Severodonetsk had population of 100,000 before Russia came. Now it’s a ghost town. That’s what Russia had been doing to every town and village that the Russian troops were sent to take, since the start of the invasion. With the exception of settlements that fell under Russian control in the first days of the invasion, other cities were turned into ruins by Russian artillery and bombs. Russian missiles can reach any city in Ukraine and during air raids, all Ukrainians have to either hide in a shelter — or find the safest place at home that might survive if the building gets hit. The air raids are usually at nights. That’s how Ukrainian kids sleep. That’s the true face of the “Russian world”. ”Russian world” means the world where Russia can attack and bomb any country they choose to attack, kill any people that Russians want to kill, for any whimsical “reason” — with impunity. ”Russian world” is the world where Russia is making rules to suit itself. ”Russian world” is where fear reins and freedom doesn’t exist. ”Russian world” is where murderers, rapists and thieves are celebrated and people who tell the truth are imprisoned and killed. “Russian world” is the absence of dignity, honor, compassion and morals. “Russian world” is total control by the state. ”Russian world” is demand for obedience and compliance. ”Russian world” makes everyone under its control complicit in its crimes. “Russian world” is where Orwell’s “1984” feels like utopia. “Russian world” is death of the soul.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: More than 76,000 Russians have been evacuated from the border region of Kursk. Are things going to plan for Putin?
Answer: The Kursk authorities left behind a veteran of WW2 that they often used for PR purposes on “Victory Day” — 98-year-old Klavdiya Tursina-Voitova from the village of Korenevo. “Everyone forgot about the only surviving participant of the Great Patriotic War, Klavdiya Tursina-Voitova. The old woman was left completely alone, and no one was going to save her. She simply turned out to be of no use to anyone,” wrote local resident Alina Belogurova. Klavdiya Tursina-Voitova went through the entire war as a medic, participated in the Battle of Stalingrad. The head of the village of Korenevo, Roman Pugachev, had previously taken photos with the pensioner for PR purposes and posted them on social networks. “Veterans are remembered only on Victory Day,” Belogurova complained. At the end, Belogurova managed to find volunteers who helped to evacuate the WW2 veteran. Russian authorities reported that 120,000 people had been evacuated in the Kursk region. But locals say that the authorities provided buses only on the first day after the advice to evacuate, and after that people had to get out on their own — or with the help of volunteers. There were also reports that the police one-off refugee support payment of 15,000 ruble promised by Vladimir Putin (a raise from the initial 10,000 rub.) — that’s about USD $150 at the current exchange rate — is nearly impossible to get. Kursk refugees also said that only these evacuated by the state on buses are eligible for the payment, and these who got out in their own can’t get it. Vladimir Putin hadn’t been saying his catch phrase “All is going according to plan” for a while. Now, Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that “the Kursk operation is going according to plan” — and unlike Vladimir Putin, Zelenskyy actually has a plan. At his latest press-conference, Zelenskyy said that he is bringing his plan how to win the war against Russia to President Biden in September — because Ukraine needs assistance from the U.S. (definitely in terms of weapons and ammunition), to be able to achieve it. "The Kursk region is included in our plan — the plan for Ukraine's victory," Zelenskyy said. He mentioned that the plan might appear too ambitious to some, but for Ukraine, it’s an important plan. The 2nd direction of the plan is "Ukraine's strategic place in the world's security infrastructure," the 3rd is "a powerful package of forcing Russia to end the war through diplomatic means," and the 4th is "economics.” After presenting the plan to President Biden, Zelenskyy plans to share his plan with both presidential candidates — Kamala Harris and Donald Trump. Meanwhile, Russia sent M-46 howitzers from 1950s to defend the Kursk region — that’s how bad the situation with weapons is in Russia. But that’s a story for another post.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How long will it take until the Russian opposition forces liberate their own nation from Putin?
Answer: All those with a voice who opposed Putin are now either in exile (had to emigrate from Russia) — or they are imprisoned in Russia. There is no political opposition to Putin within Russia left. There are a few thousand of Russian citizens in the Ukrainian armed forces who fight against the Russian army — Russian Volunteer Corps, Freedom of Russia Legion, and the Siberian Battalion — there are 3 of them, because they have different political views (yes, for real). The number of Russian citizens in the Ukrainian army is definitely not enough to “liberate their own nation from Putin”. And the Ukrainian army doesn’t have a goal to “liberate Russians from Putin.” The Ukrainian army only wants to liberate the Ukrainian territory within its 1991 internationally recognized borders. What about the Russian opposition in exile? Can these millions of Russian emigres become the force for change in Russia? Looking at the state of them, I don’t have high hopes. The state of the Russian opposition in exile is very similar to their ancestors 100 years ago — these who ran away from the Bolsheviks regime. Many of them settled in France. In mid-November 1920, not wanting to fall under the power of the Bolsheviks, about 150,000 people left Crimea by boats – mainly officers and soldiers of the White Army, as well as public officials, merchants, nobles, priests... This was perhaps the largest surge of Russian emigration in history. The Russian emigrants from 100 years ago hoped that somehow “all this horror” will end in Russia and they will be able to return, and restore the Russian Empire — as it was before October 1917. That’s what the Russian opposition in exile dreams about — to return to Russia of November 2021: The Russian opposition in exile dreams about entering the same river that had ran off 3 years ago — some even dream to return to 2011, when Putin officially got “elected” for the 3rd term — against the Constitution, when a revolution against Putin was still possible. The Russian opposition in exile has no plan how to overthrow Putin. They hoped before that Putin somehow can be voted out. Alexei Navalny gave them this hope in 2017, but he wasn’t even allowed to form a political party to be elected — and when Putin poisoned Navalny in August 2020 and then arrested him in January 2021, the most active part of the Russian opposition concentrated on trying to free Navalny from prison. Then Putin started the war in February 2022 and the oppositionists started getting arrested for speaking against the war. All vocal oppositionists either left Russia or were thrown in prison (some were killed). The evolution of the Russian oppositionists in exile during the 2.5 years of the war is remarkable (most left after the war already started). Today, I came across a thread on X-Twitter, which described the state of the Russian opposition in exile perfectly (by a Russian oppositionist in exile). ”Due to recent Durov-related events, I had way more communication with fellow Russians online than usual,” started his post Denis Zakharov. That’s Zakharov’s profile picture (yes, that’s his main profile photo, which he chose himself.) The communication with fellow Russians “was not pleasant”, admits Zakharov, pointing to a “mindset shift” that he noticed. (Below is the text by Denis Zakharov.) «…I've noticed a mindset shift, that was pretty much expected. It can be described as: “I am tired of acting like I care.” Only the most disgusting "patriots" used slurs and wished death to Ukrainians during the first year of the war. It wasn't acceptable. Until now. The new mindset of the liberal-ish Russian emigration opinion leaders looks pretty much like Trump's "America first". It starts as "we need to focus on ourselves" but nobody wants to focus on the void, so it turns into "everything behind the wall is bad and dangerous". And in the very same Trump fashion, it blooms and thrives as "we are the victims of the global conspiracy". Every day I see it growing. I watch people being proud of hating Ukrainians — even those who are opposing Putin repeat the same genocidal talking points about the evil/stupid West and Ukraine that doesn't deserve to exist. “You can stand on your knees as much as you like, you cuck [sic], it's pathetic and you lost your mind, leftie. How can you be such a cannibal to wish your own people death? We will never forgive and never forget you for that. You should feel ashamed.” I hear this a lot. It gets even more bizarre when these people who avoid Russia like wildfire call me out for being brainwashed by the West. I guess, by their logic, you can only understand The Truth about this country by being as far away as possible. But it's not a rant about degradation. Well, not only the rant. Why does this happen? Why did I expect this shift to come soon? Imagine that someone asks you to hit a wall. You say ok and hit it. And then you are asked again and again. And you hit, and you don't know why. That's what happens with people who were asked to feel guilt and shame but never took the time to think about that. "I lived a normal life and my country was OK until it wasn't and all of a sudden I AM GUILTY. ARE YOU KIDDING". From this perspective, this entire war is the act of almighty gods, the hurricane, the disaster way out of our control. And all the hatred, all the sanctions, everything that happened later is unjust and cruel. And it even could sound plausible until this recent shift. Now you can see that very same: "I came to your place, I don't like how I feel after seeing what I see. You will pay for that" mindset. "You deserve to burn and die because I am tired of being perceived as a bad guy for NO REASON". This giant glowing "NO REASON" is the reason. I remember everybody laughing at de-colonization back in 2022. I remember because I was one of those who thought that was just a funny stretch. Well, laugh now, when Russian opposition proposes Ukrainians to call them masters. I remember that moment very well when I first understood how my perception of reality was shaped by that "very funny empire". Slow Estonians, stupid Americans, barbaric Chechens, friendly yet alien Finns, little-brothers Ukrainians. It was all there, right in my head. What was not there, were the Winter War, 2 Chechen wars, famine in Qazaqstan, Latvia, and Georgia, and generations that lived a life and died while being milked and generalized and sovetized and destroyed by the country I am supposed to be proud of. It wasn't nice. Suddenly, the war was not the act of god, but a natural fallout of all the denial and casual cruelty. Hitting the gas button on the lighter and laughing "That's all the gas you ever get" to any other 12 y. o. with a Ukrainian surname. Great, Denis. Just great. It felt dreadful. The entire mindset with “the Victory Day” and “Mendeleev” and “Dostoevsky” and “mysterious Russian soul” was collapsing under the weight of new information. That nightmare where you stay naked in front of the class was basically my national id at that point. For me this is not gonna be over any time soon. You need to take the nastiest spoon and scrub this bullshit out for ages to feel at least some difference. All the "we are one nation", all the "we were better together", all the "it wasn't that bad". It was bad. We made it worse. And that's why I hate the opposition rants. They waste time by singing "Big in Japan" to an addict. Yes. 30 years of addiction will end when you choose to stop and it's gonna be just fine. No consequences. You can stop whenever you feel that's right. I am poisoned. You are poisoned. We have very little time to experience at least a fracture of normal life. And if we keep lying to ourselves, we will die in a Berlin shitter in 1983. Look at the veins of anybody who thinks I am wrong. I don't expect a happy ending. but the key to any positive change is to show what we are and what we bring with our culture, heritage and actions. *laugh track* Now I see that denial just gets worse. Thread over.» (End of quote.) Now, my thoughts. I’m not involved with the recent Russian opposition in exile — I left Russia in 1998, before Putin’s time. But it seems to me that the oppositional Russians, who were big talkers before Putin’s war of February 2022, quickly made themselves irrelevant, because they didn’t realize that things have changed — once and forever. That Russia as a state have changed and became a bona-fide dictatorship. That they have ultimately failed. And now, in my view, the only truly oppositional Russians are those fighting against Putin’s army with weapons in their hands. There are not enough of them yet. When there will be enough of them — or when Putin’s army swaps sides and becomes the anti-Putin army — then there is a chance for the Russian opposition forces to liberate their own nation (or should I say “nations”?) from Putin.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What is happening in the Kursk region of Russia?
Answer: In the Kursk region of Russia, which Ukrainian army invaded on August 6, things are moving fast. Ukraine already controls 100 settlements and the territory of 1,300 km², reported commander-in-chief Syrskyi. Time to let Ukraine take Russia! Russian military bloggers say that Ukrainian forces broke through defenses in Belgorod region — that’s the second Russian region getting invaded. Meanwhile, Russian volunteers who arrived to Kursk region with “humanitarian aid” for the Russian army (food, water, socks and jocks for soldiers, because the Russian army doesn’t provide for its troops — officers steal all the money) — so, these “volunteers” complain about traffic police cameras, which continue to send them tickets for speeding — while they are driving over the speed limits to avoid drones or shelling. The traffic police office responded that “war is war, but a violation is a violation” and fines that have already been issued in the system can only be challenged in court. You know, in Russia the law is the law! (Unless, of course, you are above the law, in which case you can break any laws you want.) I suppose, the Ukrainian tanks must have scored hundreds of fines for illegal parking. The new map of Eastern Europe has just been leaked on Telegram. On 24 February 2022, when Russia invaded Ukraine, the world was discussing how long Ukraine would be able to withstand against Russia — 2 days, 3 days, a week? Not many gave Ukraine more than 2 weeks. On August 6, 2024, when Ukraine invaded the Kursk region of Russia, Vladimir Putin ordered “to squeeze the enemy out”. On day 3, the chief of Russian general staff Gerasimov reported to Putin that the enemy had been repelled and destroyed. That was more than 3 weeks ago. Ukrainians are still in the Kursk region and keep increasing their stronghold. And now , Russians are told by their TV channels that "The incursion into Kursk region by the Ukrainians is beneficial to Russia, because it closes the conversations about negotiations with Ukraine.” Putin hopes that “the situation” in the Kursk region will somehow sort itself out, so he tries not to make a big deal about “mighty Russia” getting invaded by a “little, insignificant Ukraine.” Being invaded by a foreign power is Russia’s “new normal”.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why does Ukraine increasingly use its long-range firepower to hit oil refineries and depots deep inside Russia?
Answer: Last night, another oil depot next to a processing plant was hit in Rostov region of Russia — there are now 2 oil depots on fire: ‘Atlas’ near Molodezhny settlement, which went on fire today, and the one in Proletarsk, which is burning for 11th day. Both oil depots belong to the state strategic reserve and were holding hundreds of millions of dollars worth of fuel. Reportedly, ‘Atlas’ depot was struck by 2 Ukrainian drones: 3 tanks are burning; 2 fire trains are at the scene trying to extinguish the fire. Because of Ukraine’s attacks on oil processing plants and fuel depots, passenger planes in Russia are now put on strict limits: only 30-minute reserve of fuel is allowed per plane per flight. A pilot of a Russian airline complained that it makes flights extremely risky, because in case of a weather front or potential “drone alert” (which happen around Moscow and St. Petersburg airports fairly often), a plane may not have enough fuel to fly around, wait it out in the air or reach another air field. Fuel shortages disturb the Russian military logistics, and “eternal” multi-day fires have massive demoralizing effect on the Russian population.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Did Ukraine just test its first ballistic missile?
Answer: Ukraine had the capability to build ballistic missiles since the times of the USSR, but after signing the Budapest memorandum in 1994, Ukraine had to dispose of its arsenal of carriers of strategic nuclear warheads. Ukraine also surrendered to Russia many missiles that Putin’s army used in attacks since February 2022. So, when president Zelenskyy announced on August 27, 2024, that Ukraine has successfully tested its new ballistic missile, it was something that many analysts expected for a long time. Ukrainian journalist Dmitry Gordon (left), who was a friend of former Ukrainian president Leonid Kuchma (right) described their conversation in 2006 when Kuchma told him that Ukraine had both the capability and expertise to build ballistic missiles. Kuchma also told Gordon that Ukraine was able to build “as many as necessary” ballistic missiles. Leonid Kuchma knew what he was talking about. He began working on ‘Yuzhmash’ aerospace plant in the Ukrainian city of Dnipropetrovsk in 1960, straight after graduation from a university as an engineer. On ‘Yuzhmash’, Kuchma was working in the design bureau, where the Soviet missile systems were created. Then he moved to the position of technical director of rocket tests at the Baikonur Cosmodrome — the #1 space rocket launching pad of the USSR. During his career, Kuchma worked as a chief of both legendary flagships of the Ukrainian rocket and space industry — ‘Yuzhmash’ aerospace plant and ‘Yuzhnoye’ design bureau. For his contribution to development of rocket engineering, Kuchma was awarded the Lenin Prize in 1979 (12 years before the dissolution of the USSR). After Kuchma became the 2nd president of independent Ukraine, the first Ukrainian satellite "Sich-1" was launched into space (1995). In an interview to BBC in June 2022, Kuchma said that the latest developments of Dnepropetrovsk aerospace engineers included analogues of western weapons that Ukraine had to beg western partners for: for example, missile systems with a range of hundreds of kilometers. So, the appearance of Ukrainian-made ballistic missiles was only a matter of time — and I think Putin knew it, this is why he was in such a hurry to pressure Ukraine to sign a “peace agreement” that would prohibit further development of Ukrainian weapons. But Putin underestimated both Ukraine and the West. And now his strategic loss is obvious to anyone keeping abreast of the latest developments in this war.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Does Ukraine have mid/long-range surface-to-surface ballistic missiles? If not, why not? If so, why don't they use them?
Answer: There was the first successful test of the first Ukrainian ballistic missile, announced president Zelenskyy today. Many people don’t know that, but Ukraine was a major manufacturer of ballistic missiles during the times of the USSR. ‘Yuzhmash’ was a state-owned aerospace manufacturer in the city of Dnipropetrovsk (now Dnipro), and it’s still operational today. There is a wealth of knowledge and experience that the Ukrainian space engineers possess. In 2017, ‘Yuzhmash’ resumed production of Zenith missiles, which were intended for the use in civilian space projects. No doubt, the announcement of the Ukrainian president about the successful test of a Ukrainian-made ballistic missile is going to start an avalanche of nuclear threats from Russia. I don’t know what Putin’s goons were really thinking. That they will be hitting Kyiv and Kharkiv with ballistics for 2.5 years, and nothing will ever happen to Moscow and St. Petersburg?

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Does Russia have any Red Dawn type movies showing an American invasion?
Answer: Russians are too scared to make movies about an American invasion. In Russian movies, Americans aren’t shown as a fierce and mighty enemy — they are shown as goofy halfwits. This week, Russian TNT channel presented an upcoming series about the adventures of Joe Biden in Russia. It will be a comedy about POTUS flying to Russia incognito to understand why sanctions are not working. According to the script, the American president loses his documents, lives in a minuscule apartment, erected in a hurry during Khrushchev times, works as an English teacher and befriends a “true Russian patriot.” The series, titled “Goodbye,” will be a “kind, true-to-life, funny story,” promises actor Dmitry Dyuzhev, who is playing Joe Biden. Dyuzhev previously played a pregnant man in one of his films. In the real world of politics, "Sleepy Joe" outplayed Putin 50:0. And now, in retaliation, the Russian TV is going to mock the US president. The Russian industry of movie-making is dead. Anyone who refuses to see the reality through Putin's eyes has simply left the country. The rest resigned to filming propaganda on orders of ideologists from the presidential administration. But even in propaganda, the idea of America invading Russia (or anyone invading Russia, for that matter) is too unthinkable for Putin’s underlings. There are simply no movies like that. The only movies about a foreign invasion are from WW2 times or some other old history tales.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What are the impacts of the fires at the Proletarsk oil depot in Russia on the environment?
Answer: The fire at the strategic oil depot in the ARussian town of Proletarsk in Rostov region has been burning for 9 days, and almost all fuel had burnt out. (Video in the comments below.) But despite the smoke tail of 60 km long, the local enviromental control authorities assured residents that the quality of air was fine. Notwithstanding, the annual celebration of the Day of the City got cancelled by the administration, as well as all other outdoor activities — even though it’s the 100-year-anniversary of the district. The district administration's press service stated that the festivities were cancelled due to "the current situation in the district." (“The situation” is also the word used by Vladimir Putin to describe the Ukrainian invasion of Russia in the Kursk region.) Residents of Proletarsk complain that they have "no air to breathe" and are buying up masks to breathe filtered air. Locals are afraid to eat the vegies from their gardens: when they wash them, the water turns black. Compared to the first week of the fire, it looks like the flames are getting smaller, expectedly, as not much fuel is left. The fire began as the result of the Ukrainian drone attack on August 18. After 4 days, the local authorities even called priests to perform a prayer service, asking for divine assistance in putting out the flames. The prayers didn’t work; attempts to control the fire by firemen also didn’t work. Over 40 firemen got injured. The fuel depot had 74 giant tanks storing different types of fuel, including specific types of aviation kerosine. Russia’s ministry of emergency situations that controls the fire service didn’t post any information about the raging fire in Proletarsk, which was visible on satellite photos. The reason for the silence — not to give information to the Ukrainian Telegram channels, which would celebrate their success. At the beginning of the war, it was Russia that was destroying oil depots in Ukraine with missile strikes. Ukraine is simply paying back.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Has Omsk oil refinery, Russia's largest oil refinery just caught fire and has blown up? Gazprom, local news. How much will this affect Russia's diesel, petrol, aviation and hydrofuels? How far is Umsk from Kiev? Is Palianytsia suspected?
Answer: The explosion at the Omsk oil refinery yesterday was powerful — windows were blown out in nearby houses. According to Reuters, as a result of the explosion and subsequent fire at the Omsk oil refinery, the AVT-11 primary oil refining unit — most productive at the plant — was damaged and had to be shot down. That’s half of the plant's capacity. The fire area affected over 1,000 square meters. Omsk is about 3,000 km away from Ukraine and it’s unlikely the explosion was the result of a drone attack — although the new Ukrainian jet drone ‘Palianytsia’ can potentially fly that far, some experts believe. If Ukraine were able to hit this far (with a jet drone or another weapon), it would be a completely different reality that Russians would have to exist in.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is the use of Shahed attack drones by Russia a violation of any international laws or agreements?
Answer: Tens of 1000s of Kyiv residents rushed to hide in underground subway station this morning, as Russia sent over 109 drones and 127 missiles of various types in a massive coordinated attack on Ukrainian cities. Other Kyiv residents stayed at their homes, hiding in bathrooms and corridors with no windows near the doors in their buildings. Kyiv resident Margo Gontar posted updates for hours since 6 am: first the wait, and then listening to the horrifying sound of missiles flying over and explosions. (Video in the comments below.) “It now sounds like rolling thunder coming through the calm summer morning from several directions at once. There’s yet another air battle over the Kyiv region and many other places taking place right now,” posted Illia Ponomarenko, who lives in Kyiv region. Shelter in a maternity hospital in Rivne, where new and expectant mothers had to hide. Supposedly, the attack is in retaliation for the humiliating setbacks that Russia has faced in the Kursk region. Russia began its “special military operation” 2.5 years ago, in February 2022, under a false pretense of “protecting Russian-speaking people of Donbas.” Immediately after the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion, the general assembly of Uniate Nations recognized the attack as aggression and requested from Russia to stop it. Russia simply disregarded the UN resolution. Ukraine is a sovereign state, and Russia’s waging an aggressive war against Ukraine is against the international law and in breach of multiple treaties that Russia signed with Ukraine since 1991, when the leaders of both countries initiated the dissolution of the Soviet Union and became independents states. Clearly, Russia’s use of any weapons to hit the territory of Ukraine — military goals or not — is against international laws, agreements, treaties. But Vladimir Putin isn’t concerned about being in breach of international laws — he openly declares that Russia’s goal is to destroy the rules-based world order. Reportedly, this morning missiles managed to strike Kyiv, with explosions also heard in Chernihiv Oblast, Dnipro, Odesa, Khmelnytskyi, Kharkiv, Kryvyi Rih, Kremenchuk, Kropyvnytskyi, Myrhorod, Vinnytsia, Zaporizhia, and Lviv. 15 Ukrainian regions were targeted in one of the largest aerial attacks since the start of the full-scale war. One person was killed in Lutsk, at least one killed in Dnipropetrovsk region. The whole of Ukraine turned red on the map of air raid alerts, as missiles and drones were flying to their targets, with cruise missiles and drones changing the direction en route. According to Ukrainian media, the strikes targeted critical and energy infrastructure. Electricity has been cut off in some areas of Lviv, Khmelnytskyi, and Kyiv. There is also no water in some districts of Kyiv, power outages throughout Ukraine. Yet, Ukrainians remain resolute and stout. “If you feel rage, sadness, fury when you read my reports about russian attack on us — and if you feel you can do nothing, please think again,” Margo Gontar urged. “You can volunteer. You can donate. You can vote for politicians you trust. You can organise. You can influence others. You are so powerful.”

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Should users of Telegram be worried about the security and privacy of their messages with Pavel Durov being arrested in Paris?
Answer: Known Putin’s shills are already screaming blue murder, after the founder of Telegram Pavel Durov was arrested last night in Paris. “Backup and clean up your Telegram account while you still can,” warned wanted fugitive Kim Dotcom, who is currently fighting extradition to the U.S. for his defunct MegaUpload hub breaking IP piracy laws — the same accusation is now faced by the Telegram founder, among others. The Russian media and propagandists are blaming France, CIA, America, Zelenskyy, and everyone in between. The Russian embassy is also trying to gain access to him (although Durov previously stated he denounced his Russian citizenship; Durov left Russia after 2014). Analysts compare Durov's arrest to the British breaking the Enigma code during WW2, in its potential impact: Telegram is the most widely used messenger by the Russian army. And imagine all Russian militants’ messages getting into the hands of the West. This could also expose Russian spies in Europe. It is widely believed that the FSB has admin access to Telegram: channels that supported anti-Putin protests in Russia were promptly shut down, to prevent people from coordinating their efforts. The Kremlin is turning hysterical about the fact that "the only reliable Russian messenger may fall under control of the Western intelligence” — but at the same time mostly pushing the narrative of “freedom of speech” — and that’s coming from the country where teenagers are thrown in prison for a post in social networks, while Facebook and Instagram are officially banned. Well, Pavel Durov’s being hailed as a “free speech martyr” by the Kremlin tells you a lot. In fact, Russians don't support the Kursk Oblast as vehemently as they jumped to support Durov. Maybe, offer them to exchange Durov for Belgorod Oblast?

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What do you think will be the reaction of the Russian government to Pavel Durov's arrest?
Answer: At about 8 pm on August 24, founder of popular ‘Telegram’ app, Russian-born Pavel Durov was detained at a Paris airport on arrival. He was detained when the businessman's private jet landed at Le Bourget airport. Durov’s French properties were searched. Despite the arrest occurring at 8 pm on Saturday, the Russian authorities immediately sprang into action, demanding Durov’s release. Vice-speaker of the Russian Duma Vladislav Davankov asked the foreign minister Sergei Lavrov to intervene, and the Russian embassy in Paris has reportedly asked the French authorities to clarify the reasons why Durov was detained and asked for “consular access.” Vladislav Davankov. What is interesting, the Russian anti-Putin opposition in exile also immediately jumped to Durov’s defense, demanding his release. But the most vocal were the Russian military bloggers, who are terrified about their data potentially becoming accessible to the EU security forces. One of Russia’s top pro-war channels with 800,000 followers ironically posted, "De-facto, they detained the head of communications for the Russian Army.” Telegram is indeed the main channel of communication for the Russian military. It’s not just a source of news, but the key messenger, used to coordinate actions, store and share videos and large files, establish private chats. Russian authorities blocked Signal messenger and they are trying to block Whatsapp. Facebook and Instagram are officially banned in Russia and blocked by ISP’s. But Telegram is widely used by various Russian propagandists, including the infamous ex-proxy-president of Russia Dmitry Medvedev. Medvedev hasn’t posted anything after Durov’s arrest as yet, but it’s no surprise — after all, it’s Saturday evening we are talking about. Everyone has the right to take a break and relax. Medvedev is already under huge stress, as his giant estate that’s worth over a billion euro, is located precisely in the Kursk region, and the Ukrainian forces are getting closer every day. In the heat of the moment, Yekaterina Mizulina, a notorious Russia’s Internet watchdog (and rumored Putin’s mistress), dropped a bombshell, explaining the reason why all the Russians — both the Kremlin and the opposition in exile — might be terrified: "Durov's arrest is targeting TON cryptocurrency, which is used as a wallet by many large Russian businesspeople". Yekaterina Mizulina. TON is Telegram’s own cryptocurrency. It totally plummeted following the news of Durov’s arrest. So, the French gendarmes arrested yesterday the chief of communications of the second army in the world and the coordinator of the channels of the best propaganda in the world, AND the crypto tycoon of Moscow thieves. It’s worth noting that Pavel Durov is a French citizen and is not subject to exchange or extradition. And this leaves the question: why Durov, who spoke before about not visiting Europe fearing prosecution, suddenly decided to fly to the country where he is a citizen and can be legitimately arrested and detained? But this is a conversation for another post.

Question: Does Ukraine have a fighting chance against the Russian Army?
Answer: 2.5 years after Russia unleashed the full-scale war on Ukraine — a country 35 smaller than Russia by territory and 3.5 times smaller by population size — Ukraine celebrated its Independence Day on August 24 with massive attacks on Russian air fields and military warehouses. “Ukraine will always remain independent — this is beyond question,” said President Zelenskyy, standing at a square in the center of Kyiv, to a crowd of Ukrainians, with leaders of Poland and Lithuania present at the celebration. “Together, we have given a historic answer through our unity, courage, and collective effort. The answer to whether Ukraine should exist, and whether Ukrainians should exist,” said Zelenskyy. Russia began aggression against Ukraine in 2014, treacherously capturing and annexing Crimea, and sending troops and FSB officers to Donbas to pose as “local separatists”. When after 8 years of hybrid warfare Ukraine rejected a pro-Russian presidential candidate, Putin sent hundreds of thousands of troops to invade. The invasion was supposed to be over within 2–3 weeks — Kyiv was supposed to be taken in 2–3 days. That was the plan. And that plan failed. Ukrainians stood against Russians — and unlike in 2014, they weren’t afraid to shoot them. “When external aggression posses such a question to a nation, everything depends on millions of people — each through their actions determines the fate of the entire people, and the entire people, with their collective strength, determines the fate of each individual,” said Zelenskyy. Today, Ukrainians are more united than ever. The Russian aggression and 2.5 years of fighting invaders, facing missile attacks and mourning the loss of family and friends didn’t break Ukrainians — the gruesome tactics of Russia made Ukrainians even more determined to never allow Russia to rule over Ukraine. “A sick old man from the Red Square, who constantly threatens everyone with the red button, will not dictate any of his red lines to us,” Zelenskyy stated in his Independence Day video appeal to the nation, recorded near Ukraine’s border with the Kursk region of Russia, which Ukrainian troops invaded 2.5 weeks ago — and Putin’s army can’t do anything about it. “Only Ukraine will determine how to live, what path to take and what choice to make. Because this is how independence works,” asserted Zelenskyy, standing mere 40 km from Sudzha in the Kursk region — while Vladimir Putin isn’t only staying away from the Kursk region, he barely even mentions it, trying to downplay the fact that Russia got invaded by a foreign power and the Russian army is unable to defend it. On its 33rd Independence Day, Ukraine unleashed its superior new weapon — a jet-powered drone, named “Palyanitsia” after a type of national bread. Ukrainians already nicknamed the new weapon “drone-missile”, because of its precision and speed. The hits of new Ukrainian drones against targets in Russia started at the early hours of the morning on August 24 and continued through the day, hitting more targets in the occupied Crimea and in Russia’s Rostov region. Massive fire after a Ukrainian drone attack at Bataysk airfield near Rostov-on-Don. But instead of protecting the territory of Russia, Putin is directing the main efforts of the Russian army to advancing in Ukraine — while the incremental gains in Donbas go 10 times slower than the Ukrainian advances in Russia. To try to push the Ukrainian troops out of Russia, Russian generals ordered to bomb Russian villages occupied by the Ukrainian forces — because the only way how Russia habitually fights is to turn everything into ruins, and then send countless “meat waves” of its soldiers — with no regard to huge losses — to take over the ruins. "He [Putin] is still thinking about how to keep the occupied territories,” said Zelenskyy. “And he is not thinking about how to protect his people. Now he is bombing his villages. It's just bravo. His people there are shocked that they believed in that demon.” The main points of Zelenskyy’s Independence Day powerful video message: (Video in the comments below.) 2.5 years — very hard and testing 2.5 years for Ukraine, but how the tables have turned.

Question: Why did Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visit Ukraine?
Answer: India’s prime minister Narendra Modi brought a mobile hospital for Ukrainians, who are fighting off the Russian invasion for 2.5 years. In the book of honored guests at Kyiv’s Mariinsky Palace, Modi wrote, “On behalf of the people of India, whose population is 1.4 billion people, I pray for peace, progress and prosperity for the friendly people of Ukraine." It was the first ever visit of the head of the Indian government to Ukraine, since it gained independence in 1991. Ukraine president Zelenskyy and prime minister Modi visited the National Museum of History of Ukraine, showing the story of the Russian invasion since February 2022 and how it affected Ukrainians, particularly kids. Modi was visibly moved. Modi told Zelensky that he personally is ready to assist to achieve peace in Ukraine. India immediately "stood on the side of peace," said Modi to Zelenskyy. In a peaceful settlement, respect for sovereignty and integrity are priorities, he added. There were 4 agreements signed between India and Ukraine, covering medical field, agricultural cooperation, humanitarian relations, and culture. “Following the visit, we also agreed on a joint statement focusing on the development of a strategic partnership, bilateral trade, and continued military-technical cooperation,” posted president Zelenskyy. “India supports Ukraine's national sovereignty and territorial integrity. And this is critical because everyone in the world must equally respect the UN Charter,” Zelenskyy emphasized. Modi and Zelenskyy met previously in June in Italy during G7 summit. Following that meeting, Modi visited Putin in Russia, but cut his visit short and left one day earlier than he planned. (During Modi’s visit to Moscow, Russia hit children’s hospital in Kyiv.) Modi also met with members of the Indian community in Ukraine, who live and work there. Many Indians were going to Ukraine to study, particularly medicine and engineering. After completing their studies, some of them stayed in the country, started businesses there. At the start of the war in February 2022, 18,000 Indian students studied in Ukraine and were evacuated. Many of them since returned and now continue their studies, others are waiting until the war ends. To get a degree in Ukraine is more than twice cheaper, that’s why so many foreign students (not only from India but from many other countries) used to choose to study there. India benefited greatly from Russia’s isolated status due to western sanctions, allowing India to purchase oil from Russia at heavy discount. At the same time, India sharply decreased its purchases of Russia’s weapons and equipment, and began buying more weapons from the West. For India, western support is important, as China is striving for more influence in the region, simultaneously supplying weapons to India’s enemy Pakistan. For Ukraine, India’s support as a nation of 1.4 billion people is substantial. India has yet joined the June 2024 Swiss Peace Summit resolution, which outlined the framework of just peace for Ukraine.

Apparently, Ukrainians used a brand-new weapon to target the Voronezh site — a jet-powered drone ‘Palyanitsia’. Each of these strikes is a stroke of a global plan. We are not seeing isolated, random attempts at attacks. We are witnessing the implementation of carefully orchestrated series of operations within the framework of a single plan. What is the main goal of the plan? To force the Russian troops to leave Ukraine.

Question: Why does Russia refuse to accept equal blame for the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact and the start of WWII?
Answer: On August 23, 1939, two criminal regimes — organizers of World War 2, Germany and the Soviet Union, signed the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact and its secret protocol, defining the split of European territories between them. The pact gave the final impetus to the new world war, which began just 8 days later, with Germany’s attack on Poland. Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact: German Foreign Minister Joachim von Ribbentrop (left), Soviet leader Joseph Stalin and USSR Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov (right) on August 23, 1939 in the Kremlin after signing the pact. Stalin made a toast after the ceremony: "I know how much the German people love their Fuhrer. Therefore, I want to drink to his health." On September 1, 1939 Germany’s attacked Poland. The Soviet Union attacked Poland on September 17, 1939. On September 22, Nazis and Soviets held a joint parade in Brest, celebrating their victory. For 50 years, the USSR leaders denied that there was a secret appendix to the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact. In 1946, at the Nuremberg Trials, the former State Secretary of the German Foreign Ministry, Ernst von Weizsäcker, spoke about the existence of a secret additional protocol between the USSR and Germany. This was confirmed by other defendants, and one of the lawyers even wanted to read the text of this protocol, but he was not allowed: the USSR representatives called it a fake and said such a document never existed. In 1948, the secret protocol, based on photocopies of the German original that had not survived, was published in the US State Department collection "Nazi-Soviet Relations. 1939-1941". It also included the correspondence between Nazi and Soviet diplomats, which contained references to secret agreements. But the Soviet Union continued to claim that this was a falsification, that no additional secret appendix to the 1939 agreements ("On Non-Aggression" and "On Friendship and Borders") between the USSR and Germany existed. Moreover: in response to the publication by the State Department, Moscow published its own work titled "Falsifiers of History". But it did not contain a single complete copy of a document, only a few fragments. Stalin didn’t want to be blamed in starting the World War with Hitler, and used the status of the USSR as one of the “victors of WW2” to suppress this extremely important information. Molotov, who signed the non-aggression pact and the secret protocol to it, denied its existence until his death in 1986. Minister of Foreign Affairs of the USSR Vyacheslav Molotov in Berlin, November 14, 1940. It was hard to prove that such a document existed: one party that signed it (Hitler's Germany) no longer existed, and the other (the Soviet Union) denied that it existed at all, and had no intention of publishing it. Only in 1989, the Soviet leaders admitted that such secret protocol existed, on request of representatives of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. A copy of the German document was published in the USSR. The actual copy of the secret protocol in Russian was first kept in Stalin's safe and then in the archive of the Central Committee of the Communist Party. In 1992, after the dissolution of the Soviet Union, the archive of the Communist Party was declassified and the secret protocol was discovered. From that moment, the existence of a secret additional treaty to the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact had become a reliably recognized fact not only in the West, not only in the Baltic countries, Moldova and Ukraine, but also in Russia itself. But now, Putin’s propaganda downplays the importance of the secret agreement between Hitler and Stalin how they would divide Europe, and overemphasizes that it was a non-aggression pact, which allowed the USSR 2 more years without the war. Completely disregarding the fact that without the secret agreement to split European lands, there possibly wouldn’t happen such a war. Putin went much further than Stalin — he now claims it was Russia that defeated Hitler (not even the USSR but Russia), and the whole world must be grateful to Russia for defeating the Nazi regime. Putin’s propaganda promoted this idea for years, having convinced some westerners that Russia was some kind of “savior” nation. And then Putin used this notion to attack Ukraine: he labeled Ukrainians “Nazis” and sent the Russian troops to invade Ukraine “to defeat a Neo-Nazi regime”. Putin hoped it would work and the world would buy into it. He still hopes he can convince us.

Question: Is the president of Ukraine banning Christianity and closing churches in his country?
Answer: Yesterday, the Ukrainian parliament voted to ban the FSB Moscow church in Ukraine — after 2.5 years of the full-scale war and 10.5 years since Russia annexed Crimea. But finally, it’s done! By no means it means that “Ukraine bans Christianity”. All Christian confessions — including the Orthodox Christianity — are allowed in Ukraine, none are being “banned”. What is severed, however, is the churches subordination to Moscow Patriarchate. It’s been long overdue, but after much deliberation and explanatory work to Christians worldwide, the Ukrainian lawmakers finally voted to approve it. Since the beginning of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, many Moscow-appointed priests were acting on orders of their FSB curators. As of May 2024, Ukraine still had about 8,000 communities that were part of the Moscow Patriarchate. Now these communities will have to cut ties with Moscow, and join Ukraine's own Christian Orthodox Church, which had been created in 2018 and blessed by the Holy Synod of the Patriarchate of Constantinople, the worldwide leadership of Orthodox Christianity. In 2022-2023, about 1,000 communities have already disassociated from Moscow and joined the Orthodox Church of Ukraine. Once again: the law gives 9 months to all Christian Orthodox communities to cut the ties to Moscow. What happens if they don’t? Then the government and the church have to go to court, and it will probably take years until any orders are given as to what to do with these communities. These churches will not be shut down and will continue operating until such time the court makes its determination. The Ukrainian government obviously understands that it’s a sensitive matter and acts in good faith, yet with full realization of the fact that it has the utmost obligation to protect the national security. In fact, it wasn’t Ukraine that cancelled the Russian church in its country. By invading Ukraine and killing tens of thousands of Ukrainians, it was Russia that “cancelled” itself and its institutions in Ukraine.

Answer: Brothers Kiskorov — Gennady and Semyon — who were mobilized into the Russian army in 2022, tried to refuse orders of their commanders, and now one of them is dead and the other one cannot be found. The Kiskorovs are from the Kemerovo region. They are Shors by nationality — it’s a small nation, there are only about 13,000 of them left in the Russian Federation. When Putin announced mobilization in the fall of 2022, like many other national minorities, Shors were drafted with particular zeal. Analysts already pointed out that indigenous peoples of Russia were practically massacred in this war via military recruitment. Semyon and Gennady ended up in the 74th Motorized Rifle Brigade that was sent to Donetsk region. Gennady (top) and Semyon with their wives. In mid-2023, the brothers refused to continue to fight and demanded a switch to an alternative civilian service, citing their religious beliefs. There were several “refuseniks”, at first they were sent to work as military builders. But then an order was given to get them back into the storm troops. Because they still refused to fight, the brothers were tortured and tied to a tree. Being tied to a tree is a typical punishment in units stationed on the occupied territory of Ukraine near the front: a person is kept tied up without food or water for days — in the best traditions of the Russian army. Sometimes the handcuffs were nailed to a tree, so the person couldn’t even sit down. The commanders told the brothers that they would anyway be sent to an assault, but if they didn’t agree to fight, they would be pushed on the battlefield with no support, to a certain death. The brothers were also separated and assigned to different units. Once, Semyon managed to film a video of how a man in his unit was being tied to a tree. Semyon posted the video to his family at home and in social networks. He also gave an interview to journalists of a Russian opposition TV channel that broadcasts from Europe. Very quickly after that, he was called to the commander and forced to withdraw the application that he made to the military prosecutor's office and delete his posts. The last thing Semyon managed to tell his family was that the commanders threatened him that he would also be tied to a tree, or transferred to the unit of kamikaze stormtroopers. After that, both brothers disappeared. Only recently did the family learn that Semyon was killed, apparently around the same time, in December 2023. The place and circumstances of his death are unknown. His body was delivered in a closed coffin, and the family was forbidden to open it. The state said he was identified by the DNA, supplied by his mother, and his body tag. The coffin was delivered to the family in August 2024. What happened to his brother Gennady is unknown. Most likely, he perished in pointless “meat attacks” or in one of the many "pits" where commanders throw ”refuseniks”. Extrajudicial punishments in the Russian army are now perceived as a norm. The Russian state does not react in any way to complaints of soldiers about their commanders. Soldiers in the Russian army are viewed and treated worse than slaves — especially the mobilized (as compared to volunteers on a contract). The Russian military and the office of prosecutor refused to investigate the circumstances of death and disappearance of the brothers. No matter what the families of the forcibly mobilized soldiers do and which government bodies they try to appeal to, their loved ones end up either in a “pit” on the occupied Ukrainian territory or dead. Once the army has you in its claws, there is no way out. The whole Russian army is one giant war crime machine. And the torture engine is what keeps it going.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Will the Ukrainian offensive into Kursk (within Russia) change the outcome of the war? What is the purpose?
Answer: TAP ON THE PHOTO TO VIEW. For a long time, I was thinking that if the West abandoned Ukraine, they would simply send troops to take Moscow, Prigozhin-style. I never voiced this thought, because I’m not a military strategist — I’m just reporting on the news that get traction in the Russian-speaking social media space. But the obvious fact that the Russian territory has been left barely protected because all troops and weapons that Russia has are sent to Ukraine was an open secret. So, when Ukraine was put into the situation where they felt pressured into “peace negotiations” with Russia — based on the paradigm of “taking in consideration the situation on the ground” (which implied that Ukraine would have to surrender territories occupied by the Russian army) — they made the most logical move and changed that “situation.” Putin has no answer to this new “situation on the ground”. That’s why he never said anything about Kursk since the first days when it was still treated as a raid. That’s why all Putin-lovers suddenly stopped their preaching about “peace negotiations”. Zelenskyy now repeats exactly the same phrases that Putin was feeding the media for 2.5 years: “all operational goals are being achieved”, “all is going according to plan”, “buffer zone”, and so on. And the most important strategic goal — calling Putin’s bluff about so called “red lines” — has already been achieved. Russia is invaded, its sovereignty threatened, its territory being hit with western weapons, western tanks are roaming the Russian land — and Putin hasn’t done anything he threatened he would do. Moreover, it looks like Ukrainian forces have a good chance of capturing the Kursk nuclear power plant — Russia still controls Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia NPP — and this would make Ukraine’s negotiation position even stronger. At the same time, the operation in Kursk provided an enormous boost for Ukrainians’ morale and reinvigorated trust in the Ukrainian leadership among the population, which will be surely seen in the next public opinion polls. It had exactly the opposite effect on Russians. Now the rumor has it, Putin ordered to push out the Ukrainian troops from the Kursk region by October 1. This shows how badly is Russia prepared to defend its own territory — but we also know how the Russian army fights: they turn everything into ruins with bombs and artillery. This means, the Russian army now will be bombing its own territory, its own citizens. I’m sure this will create an even more acute PR disaster for Putin, and all Russian regions South-West of Moscow — and Moscow itself — would be fearing the same fate. Kursk invasion was a stroke of genius.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How can I immigrate to Russia?
Answer: To those souls out there who dream of immigrating to Russia, a surefire opportunity just opened up: Vladimir Putin signed a decree that allows westerners to get a residence permit in the Russian Federation. All you have to do is to claim asylum on the basis of suffering from “destructive liberal attitudes.” Yes, for real. So, from now on, foreigners who "share traditional Russian spiritual and moral values" — even without knowledge of the Russian language — can move to Russia. Vladimir Putin signed a decree that citizens of countries whose governments "impose destructive liberal attitudes" will be able to obtain a residence permit in Russia — obviously, this doesn’t mean citizens of countries like Iran or Somali, but these from Europe or the USA — gullible enough to seek in Russia the bastion of “traditional values”. ”Form an orderly queue,” celebrated the news known Kremlin shills. No kidding.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How has the element of surprise impacted Ukraine's incursion into the Kursk region?
Answer: At a meeting with foreign diplomates, Ukraine President Zelenskyy said that Ukrainians kept quiet about the offensive in the Kursk region of Russia because it might have appeared unrealistic. "Just a few months ago, upon hearing that we were planning such an operation in Kursk Oblast, many representatives of the international community would have said that it was unrealistic and it crossed Russia’s main red line,” said Zelenskyy. “This is why nobody had been informed about our preparations. Now the real success speaks for itself: our active defensive actions on the other side of the border and Putin’s inability to protect his territory from our defensive actions of this kind are very telling." Truth is, most likely the Ukrainians kept quiet about the plan to invade Russia because they had experience of their plans leaked to Russians. One of previous operations was reportedly cancelled because Russians found out about the plan, and the big offensive of 2023 didn’t turn out well for Ukraine because Russians knew where the Ukrainian forces planned to attack. Apparently, only commander-in-chief Syrskyi and president Zelenskyy himself, along with a few top generals, knew about the plan. Even the people in the office of the Ukrainian president didn’t know: Syrskyi talked to Zelenskyy 1-to-1. The Main Intelligence Directorate (GUR) didn’t participate in planning the Kursk operation; the army used its own intel. The soldiers of the Ukrainian forces found out about the operation just hours before. In the briefing for foreign diplomates, Zelenskyy explained that right now a huge ideological change is occurring: "The whole naive illusory concept of Russia’s so-called ‘red lines’, which prevailed in some partners’ assessment of the war, crumbled somewhere near Sudzha over these few days." “Now the world sees that it is realistic, that it really works. Not only in the temporarily occupied territory of our country but in the territory of Russia as well. The world sees that everything in this war depends only on courage — our courage, and the courage of our partners,” said Zelenskyy. All we need is courage. And weapons.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why did Muscovy change its name to Russia?
Answer: ”Russia” is the English word; in reality, the name of the state that Muscovy principality decided to adopt as the name of its empire was “Rossia”. “Rossia” is the Greek word for “Rus” — the name of the historical Slavic state with the capital in Kyiv. The USSR historians began calling it “Kievan Rus”, because in the Soviet history books the history of the USSR was starting with 9th century Rus. The legend of Kyiv being founded in 482 by brothers Kyi, Shchek, Khoryv and their sister Lybid was also included. By adopting the name “Rossia” (Russia) Muscovy princes laid their claim on the lands that belonged to Ukraine. 1709 newspaper “The Daily Courant” talks about Muscovy and Ukraine. The decision to change the name from the principality of Muscovy to the Russian Empire was political, and, as it was customary at the time, accompanied by forged history, backing the claim. In our times, Vladimir Putin, the ruler of the Russian Federation, is also forging history, trying to lay claim on the territories outside of the internationally recognized Russia’s borders. 17th century thinking in the 21st century. Insane.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What can Russia do at this point to end Ukraine's surprise cross-border attack on the Kursk border region?
Answer: TAP ON THE PIC TO VIEW. The recipe to end the war in Ukraine remains the same since day #1: Russia needs to get the heck out of Ukraine. There is no need for any military genius to try to come up with ideas. The one and only solution for Russian generals has been on the table all along. Putin’s “special military operation” in Ukraine was supposed to last weeks, maximum a month. Kyiv was supposed to fall in 3 days, Russian special forces were tasked with capturing the Ukrainian leadership on the day when the Russian invasion of Ukraine started — February 24, 2022. It’s been obvious for 2.5 years that this plan had failed. And it’s been obvious for months that Putin’s next plan — to exhaust Ukrainians and make them give in, constantly demanding “peace negotiations that recognize the realities on the land” wasn’t going to work either. Ukraine's surprise cross-border attack on the Kursk region — and the fact that Ukrainians are planning to keep the stronghold over the captured territory — put an end to such hopes. It also demonstrated the complete ineptitude of the Russian army, both of its intelligence and the ground troops. Yet, the political decision of Russia’s leadership to end the war in Ukraine by the only reasonable way available to them — withdrawing their troops from the internationally recognized territory of Ukraine — still hadn’t been made. Putin’s gang intends to kill tens of thousands more Russian men — including 18–19-year-old teenage conscripts on compulsory 1-year military service — to keep the waning hope of expanding the Russian empire alive. Vladimir Putin is consciously throwing tens of thousands of lives of Russian citizens into the oven of his ambitions. He will keep doing it until the end. His end, the end of the Russian Federation, or the end of patience of his subjects — whichever comes first.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How did the myth of the mighty Russian Army start?
Answer: In Nizhny Novgorod region, mobilized soldiers who were wounded are being handcuffed to a radiator in a decaying prison building. They get beaten and abused for refusing to go back to the front in Ukraine. (Video in the comments below.) Such treatment is supposed to motivate them to agree to go back to the war. At the front in Ukraine, “refuseniks” are casually shot; on the territory of Russia, they are abused and tortured by hunger, beaten, often raped. “The mighty Russian army” doesn’t exist. It never existed. There was the Soviet army, which was also built on fear, brainwashing and propaganda — but there was something else. The Soviet people who fought against Hitler troops in WWII — and prevailed, were fighting to repel the enemy and kick out the invaders from their land. This isn’t what the Russian army is doing in Ukraine — it’s not what the Russian army was doing in Georgia or Syria. No one invaded the Russian Federation since it became a country in 1991. “Every war is terrible, and the Russian-style war is ugly,” writes Mykhailo Podolyak, advisor to the office of the president of Ukraine. “Without a pity for your own and others, when destruction is preferred to capturing. The deserts scorched by Russian bombs on our land will take decades to heal. Some cities will not be rebuilt. Missile and bomb attacks on hospitals, rape of people regardless of gender and age, abduction of children, executions of prisoners and their own refuseniks – the real ‘Gerasimov Doctrine’ has turned crimes into a tactic of war,” says Podolyak. That’s the only way that the Russian army under Putin knows. They are unable to fight differently, the whole Russian army is one giant war crime. And that’s how they are trying to fight against Ukraine’s invasion in the Kursk region. “Now Putin's army is fighting on the territory of RF, shelling and storming Russian cities and towns. Russian pilots are destroying civilian infrastructure in the Kursk region with multi-kilogram bombs, forcing tens of thousands of local residents to leave their homes. Russian soldiers are looting shops and civilian homes of their neighbors,” describes Podolyak. Before, Russians were watching the war as a television show, but for hundreds of thousands of Kursk region residents, the war is now becoming close and personal. And they can feel and experience what the Ukrainian residents living near the border with Russia had been living through for years. This new reality terrifies them. As is the fact that “the mighty Russian army” can’t protect them.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Has the surprise Ukrainian incursion caused chaos in the Kursk region?
Answer: The residents of territories taken over by the Ukrainian troops in the Kursk region are terrified and bitter, and warn Russians to don’t believe anything they see on TV (video in the comments below). The administration and government services were the first to run away, often leaving documentation behind. In the local police, folders with criminal cases against local residents who escaped military enlistment were left behind — the Ukrainian soldiers burned them. Avoiding mobilization is a crime punishable by 10 years in prison in Russia. Ukrainian forces knocked out the last remaining bridge over the Seim river, destroying 3 out of 3 bridges connecting the area with the rest of the Kursk region — practucally cutting off the Glushkovsky district: a 700 square km triangle has the Ukrainian border on one side, Ukrainian troops on the other side, and river on the third side. Reportedly, around 2,700 Russian soldiers and officers are now cut off on that territory. In social networks, locals are looking for dinghies and blow up boats, to enable them to cross the Seim River. “Don’t believe what they say on TV,” urge Sudzha residents their compatriots, adding that “no one is telling the truth.” Despite the Russian media giving a heavily moderated version of “events in the Kursk region” (Putin called it “a situation”), Muscovites are starting to get worried. “Guys, honestly I've been scared this whole week. I'm scared that my house will be destroyed, I'm in shock. Kursk region is 500 km from Moscow. And how do people with children live? Are they doubly scared? I don't know what to do, I'm a coward and a nervous wreck,” writes one girl. ”Let our Crimea become a grave for you. For you and other occupiers. May all of you die for this Ukrainian peninsula that you needed so much. I won't even mention the tens of thousands of kilometers of scorched earth. Stock up on gloves — you'll need them to clear the rubble at home and for digging out your neighbors. Greetings from Donetsk,” responded a Ukrainian who had to run away from the Russian occupation twice — in 2014 from Donetsk and in 2022 from the Kyiv region. Washington Post reporters visited Sudzha and talked to a dozen of locals. Sudzha residents said that they have been treated well by the Ukrainian soldiers and do not know of any residents killed. But they still want things to be back as they were. Despite them living right next to the border and the war with Ukraine raging for over 2.5 years, they never thought it would reach them. One man said he wants Putin to come to an agreement with Zelenskyy, so that “everything is resolved in a good way”. One man said he wanted to find his daughter in Kharkiv (Ukraine), whom he couldn’t see since the start of the war. “We want peace and harmony. We don't want anything else; we don't care for anything else,” said another woman. “Please help us,” she begged WP reporters. “But we are just civilians,” kept saying Sudzha residents. So were the Ukrainians who live under Russian bombs and missiles for 2.5 years. No place in Ukraine is safe — nowhere in the whole of Ukraine. Russia can hit any town or village with their long-range missiles and drones. Sudzha residents asked reporters to send photos of the destroyed buildings in their town to Vladimir Putin. They still believe that he would help them. Not sure if the reporters told them that Putin is too busy — he’s laying wreaths in Baku, Azerbaijan, and dining with the country’s ruler and his wife, thousands of miles from the Kursk region.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is there running inflation currently in Russia? How are people coping with it?
Answer: Residents of regional Russian towns are the first to experience the mighty hit of running inflation. On July 26, 2024, Russia raised the base rate to 18.00% per annum. The central bank of Russia explained that “inflation has accelerated and is significantly higher than the April 2024 forecast,” but talks about the need to raise the base rate had been ongoing for months — the rate was kelp at “low” 26% per annum to allow for Putin’s re-election and inauguration. Life has become more expensive in Russia within the last year: At the same time, there is nearly no money for increases in wages in the state budget — all money goes to war. With the running inflation, interest rates for home loans in Russia are over 20%. Russia is turning into a giant Ponzi scheme that’s doomed to collapse.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What could be the reason that the much-loved leader of Russia is now visiting Azerbaijan? Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Azerbaijan's capital Baku on Sunday for a two-day state visit. He hasn't been there since 2018. Weapons?
Answer: Some suggested that Putin flew to Azerbaijan to design a way around western sanctions to sell Russian oil and gas, others pointed out that Putin prefers to be away when things within Russia get tricky and there is a need to arrest some high-up officials. In July 2024, it was reported that “the EU opened talks with Azerbaijan to replace more Russian gas exports to Europe.” Ukraine's deal to transport Russian gas expires at the end of 2024, and last week the Ukrainian troops captured the gas measuring station in Sudzha, Kursk region of Russia, which controls the pipe from Russia to Europe via Ukraine. Putin might be offering Aliev a deal to sell Russian gas masking it as Azerbaijani gas, for a cut. But there could be another reason: Putin might have flown to Baku to meet his Israeli doctors, who refused to travel to Moscow. The rumor originated from Baku social media. Azerbaijan is friendly with both Moscow and Israel, so it could be viewed as a neutral platform. At the same time, there were reports that Azerbaijan moved its air defence units to the border with Iran, supposedly to help in shooting down Iranian missiles in case of an attack on Israel. Iran supports Armenia, and Armenia and Azerbaijan are sworn enemies — just a year ago, Azerbaijan took back territories that were occupied by Armenia (with the help of Russia) since early 1990s. Russia is getting drones and missiles for the war in Ukraine from Iran, and is indebted to the regime of ayatollahs. Maybe Putin is there to try to convince the Azerbaijan’s leader to help Iranians by doing nothing. Notably, Putin hadn’t been met at the airport by Azerbaijan president Aliev, but by the vice prime minister. Although Aliev did meet Turkey president Erdogan at the airport, when the Turkish leader visited Baku. Photos of Putin with the Alievs were made later. Putin, Aliev and his wife were all grinning happily, which probably would look out of place for 200,000 residents of the Kursk and Belgorod regions who had to evacuate from their homes, because the Russian territory is invaded by Ukraine. But what can Putin do if there is always something seriously wrong in Russia? Can’t a ruler take a break from all these mourning faces he has to see every day around himself in Russia? If you were living in 2024 Russia, you’d also crave some normality — even if only for a couple of days.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Did Russia ever report military losses?
Answer: On August 19, 2024, Russia’s military losses in the war with Ukraine have reached 600,000 — but you won’t find such reports in the Russian media. The last time Russia reported its losses was nearly 2 years ago, in September 2022 (6 months into the war), and back then the minister of defense Sergei Shoigu stated that less than 6,000 Russian soldiers were killed in Ukraine. Since then — even if we believed Shoigu (the numbers were misleadingly low, in my view) — since then, the tactic of “meat waves” was implemented by Russia, to break through the Ukrainian defence lines, which means the Russian losses were certainly higher over similar periods of time, not lower. Russian oppositional outlet Mediazona identified with names nearly 62,000 Russian soldiers and officers killed in Ukraine. According to MediaZona, the real number of Russian KIA would be around 120,000. I believe that 120,000 Russian KIA is a very conservative estimate, because many Russian soldiers are shot by their own commanders for refusing to fight, as well as by barrier troops. Many Russian soldiers evacuated from the battlefield die in hospitals. With the recent desperate attempts of the Russian army to advance in the Donetsk and Kharkiv regions, daily losses — as reported by Ukrainians — rarely show numbers below 1,000. These losses include killed, seriously wounded and captured by the Ukrainian army. It’s worth noting that to report a number of personnel or equipment losses, Ukrainians require a video confirmation. So, the numbers reported by the Ukrainian side, while appear high, are based on factual evidence. Russia is under enormous stress due to the war, and personnel losses of mostly young and middle-aged males are substantial for the country with the aging population. The fact that Putin is now throwing in 18–19-year-old conscripts trying to stop the Ukrainian invasion in the Kursk region speaks for itself — Russia doesn’t have a reserve of trained professional troops. Learning about the size of the actual losses would be a shock for the Russian public.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How could Ukraine invading the Kursk region in Russia be an embarrassment to President Vladimir Putin?
Answer: Vladimir Putin’s plane landing in Kursk, to support the region in fighting off Ukraine’s invasion. JUST KIDDING!! Putin flew to Baku, Azerbaijan, while 18–19-year-old Russian conscripts are flown by military planes to the Kursk region from all over Russia. Putin never goes to where problems in Russia happen — be it a major flood or an invasion by a foreign power. Putin doesn’t want to associate himself with disasters. He only wants to associate himself with victories. Putin needs to redirect attention from the invasion of Kursk and Belgorod, and the meager response provided by the Russian military. For 2 weeks, Russia — a nuclear power — cannot repel foreign troops that invaded its territory. Moreover, that’s another “red line” crossed — and nothing is happening! The world realized that there are no “red lines”. The king is naked. And this is obvious not only to westerners but also to Russian citizens who previously believed the TV, promoting Russia’s “greatness”. Moreover, Kursk locals who didn’t evacuate, got to see Ukrainians, fighting against the Russian army. They saw that they are not “Nazis”, but normal guys, who are also handing out humanitarian aid — food, water. They also saw that the local administration and police were the first to run away, leaving them alone with the "enemy". That there was no evacuation. They also saw how the Russian TV was showing completely different scenes. People saw that they are being lied to. Mothers of Russian conscripts who are serving the compulsory 1-year-term of military service got a shock of their lives that their sons can be placed in mortal danger, despite many promises made by Vladimir Putin that conscripts won’t be involved in combat. There are about 350,000 conscripts in the Russian army and they all have mothers, fathers, siblings, grandparents. All these families are now terrified that their teens who were promised that they wouldn’t be fighting the Ukrainians, could be fed into the meat grinder of the war. Despite Putin’s hopes and requests of Duma members, there are no queues to army recruitment centers to “defend the Russian land from invaders”. And this must be the most embarrassing thing for Putin.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Putins asks Russian women to give birth to 7-8 kids per woman and also asks for another 170,000 soldiers. Is there a correlation? Is Russia's relatively small population enough?
Answer: This photo is real — only translated by Google Lens. The original is in the comments below. That’s an ad in Russia asking women to have kids: “The time has come!” says the ad, using a derogatory word for women (instead of “dames” or “ladies”). On top of the ad, it says “Russia’s National Projects” — “Demographics”. The baby is in hands of a military veteran, wearing 4 “Hero” stars. A Russian national project of baby-making. To understand the level of cringeworthiness, this ad is displayed right now in Kursk.
