The city that hears several air raids per day, because the Ukrainian army invaded the Kursk region 2 weeks ago — and the Russian army can’t push them out, because there are only untrained 18–19-year-old conscripts and Kadyrov’s Tik-Tok troops. By now, 2,000 thousand of these untrained conscripts, who are serving their compulsory 1-year military service term — along with some Kadyrov’s Tik-Tok troops — have been captured by the Ukrainians, which is rapturing into a scandal in Russia. Putin sent professional troops to invade Ukraine 2.5 years ago — and by now most of them are dead. The army contractors that Putin managed to attract for the war in Ukraine (by either threats or promises of big wages) comprise of prisoners, criminals, alcoholics and debtors — the bottom of the barrel, but even these guys, who are ready to kill for money, aren’t available to defend Russian land in Kursk — Putin sent them to capture ruins of Ukrainian towns in Ukraine, and he doesn’t want to move them back to Russia — Putin is obsessed with Ukraine. Duma members scolded Kursk residents and told them that the state has no obligation to defend them. And that they should be joining the army — all the while as the face of a smiling general holding a baby looks at them from posters, demanding from women to have kids. In July 2024, the number of deaths in Russia was 20% higher than a year ago. That’s the cost of Putin’s war.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Did you see any Russian soldiers surrendering to Ukrainians?
Answer: Videos of surrendering Russian soldiers are flooding Internet, after Ukraine’s surprise advance in the Kursk region. Foreign journalists visited Russians, captured in the Kursk region, in a Ukrainian prison and asked them questions. Some were happy to talk, some refused. In just one prison, there were 250 Russian conscripts serving their compulsory 1-year military service, who were assured they wouldn’t be sent into a combat zone. “Motherland will always lie to you, son.” A group of Russian conscripts surrendered to the Ukrainians to avoid being killed by Kadyrov’s guys. They were soldiers of the 488th Motorized Rifle Regiment. They were unable to withstand against Ukrainian forces advancing on tanks and started retreating, but were shot at by Kadyrov’s guys. To understand the role of Kadyrov’s guys, they are part of “Rosgvardia” (Russian National Guard), which are troops under command of the president of Russia, not the Ministry of Defence. They are deliberately placed behind the regular troops, to shoot at them if anyone tries to run back. So, in fact, Kadyrov’s guys are “barrier troops”. The reason why they are given the job of barrier troops is because they feel no pity shooting retreating Russians. Kadyrov’s guys have a reputation among the regular Russian troops who try to stay away from them even on a good day. That’s why whole units of Russians are surrendering — they choose between certain death under fire from Kadyrov’s “barrier troops” and the Ukrainian captivity. Some obviously die under fire, and some manage to surrender. (Surrendering on the battlefield is not easy, but because it’s not a regular situation and Russians were taken by surprise, Ukrainians made it possible.) So, the Russians first allowed — and even helped — Kadyrov’s guys to build a “reputation”, and now they are furious with young 18–19-year-old untrained conscripts for surrendering to Ukraine. And now the mothers of these conscripts are starting to make noise — because Putin promised several times that conscripts serving their compulsory 1-year term of military service won’t be used in combat on SMO (special military operation). But this protest won’t last, of course. The mothers will be quickly silenced with either bribes or threats, and we’ll never hear about them again. That’s why Putin named Ukraine’s Kursk offensive “a situation” and ordered to conduct “a counter terrorist operation” (CTO) there. It’s not SMO, it’s CTO. So, shut up. And stop creating panic — everything is under control. Or we’ll arrest you for “discrediting the Russian army”, and lock you in prison for 15 years. What is weird, Putin’s regime spends so much time and effort to make things appear “right”, they don’t have time or ability to put enough effort into making things right. And that’s why Russia can’t win the war in Ukraine.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How is the Russian counter offensive going in Kursk to throw out the Ukrainian Armed Forces?
Answer: TAP ON THE PHOTO TO VIEW. “The operation in the Kursk region is going according to plan,” assured President Zelensky. As for the master strategist Putin, it’s the 905th day of his special military operation. And he still thinks he can win. Talk about grandiose delusions.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What is the name of the new Kursk Republic? Is it Kursk People's Republic or just Kursk Republic? When is the referendum for the separation from the Russian Pederation? Have you seen the flag of this new country?
Answer: The flag of the new Kursk People’s Republic has been revealed. Ukrainian soldiers have been putting up flags of the soon-to-come KuPR on administrative buildings, to further highlight the fact that Ukraine doesn’t plan to occupy or keep Russian lands. Notice the building is NOT bombed into ruins. That’s the drastic difference of Ukrainian troops taking over the Russian territory — Ukrainians capture settlements with buildings intact, while Russians bomb towns into oblivion, and put up the Russian tricolor over the ruins. Even though Vladimir Putin announced many times that “Russia has no borders”, Ukraine respects international borders and doesn’t intend to annex the territory it captured from Russia. But for the moment, the territory needs governing, so Ukrainians establish military administration, the main task of which is to assist remaining civilians with food and water, as well as help them to evacuate, if they wish. There is also a 24-hour hotline for those on occupied Russian territories, who need supplies or wish to evacuate. The Russian civilians of the Kursk region can safely evacuate to the Sumy region of Ukraine. There is also an option of evacuating towards Russia, as Ukraine is open to providing humanitarian corridors. The operation in Kursk is ongoing for 12 days, since August 6. For nearly 2 weeks, Russia is unable to “squeeze out” the Ukrainian troops from its land, and the size of the territory captured by Ukraine in Russia increases every day. The size of the territory seized by Ukraine in Russia will soon equal the size of Gagauzia, one of 2 pockets created by Russia on the border between Ukraine and Moldova. The territory of Gagauzia: 1,832 km². The territory of Transnistria: 4,163 km². Russia is always creating 2 abscesses on borders of countries it wishes to control: they’ve done the same in Georgia and Ukraine. Maybe it’s time for Russia to taste its own medicine.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is Russia’s talk of Ukraine using a dirty bomb on its own territory indicate that Russia may be planning to use a dirty bomb themselves and blame it on Ukraine?
Answer: ‘Russia Today’, TASS, and RIA Novosti, as well as all the Putin’s shills are posting and reposting each other, threatening that “Ukraine is going to blow a dirty bomb in Eastern Europe.” Is Russia going to blow a dirty bomb somewhere and blame it on Ukraine? Hell, no. Putin is embarrassed that his troops can’t stop the Ukrainian offensive in the Kursk region, and it makes him look pathetic. So, Putin’s administration is trying to eclipse the global news about Ukraine’s success in invading Russia by scaremongering: even if no one believes that Ukraine would drop a “dirty bomb”, they might start worrying that it’s Putin who is planning to do it, and the incessant chatter is the Kremlin’s coverup tactic. To remind you: Russians have done it before, they’ve threatened a “Ukrainian dirty bomb”, to overshadow undesirable news. Putin’s propagandists are terrified to try something new in a crisis — in case it doesn’t work and the author of the idea moves next in line for a hexa-share Lefortovo cell. That’s why Russian propagandists prefer to reapply tried and tested methods: dirty bomb, bio laboratories, WW3 — and so on, ad nauseam. Because it would be stupid to make nuclear threats in the current situation — Russia is being invaded right now! It would be time to walk the walk — not talk the talk, if Russia’s nuclear blackmail were even 0.5% truthful. Even Medvedev — who loves nuclear bluff — had shut up, and is only squealing about “illegal border crossing” and “terroristic nature of the neo-Nazi regime” (yes, for real). So, what’s next on the list, after the nukes? “A dirty bomb” — sounds just as worrisome. Just another PR caper by Kremlin shills.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Does Russia have everything under control when it comes to the Kursk situation?
Answer: Things aren’t looking good for Vladimir Putin, with Ukraine’s surprise Kursk offensive becoming a major slap in the face for the Russian dictator. It is 11th day of the Ukrainian incursion in the Kursk region, and by now it’s revealed something strategically important: the Russian Federation does not have an army to "advance all the way to the English Channel" as they threatened. Sure, Russian troops can raze to the ground Ukrainian villages in Donbas with their aerial bombs and fill them with corpses of their stormtroopers, thrown in “meat attacks” by Russian commanders with no pity or count. They can still fire missiles at Ukrainian cities, although most of them get shot down. But Russia does not have an army to defend its own territory. It was first shown by Yevgeny Prigozhin, who managed to pass with a military convoy nearly all the way to Moscow (shooting down Russian planes and helicopters as they went). And now it’s shown by the Ukrainian armed forces. Even in the fortified border regions with Ukraine, after 10.5 years of the military conflict — and 2.5 years of the full-scale war, even there the Ukrainians just rolled in and Russians began surrendering by hundreds. Truly embarrassing for Putin — and it can get worse.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Does the world know the Kursk offensive was nothing more than a PR stunt by Ukraine, in order to manufacture some type of hope for more funding?
Answer: “Ukrainian offensive in Kursk is just a PR stunt” was the first stage of denial for Putin’s propagandists. After that, they began reporting about “destroyed enemy forces” and “the situation has been stabilized.” For over 10 days since August 6, Ukraine keeps advancing and enlarging the area under control. Yesterday, a key bridge over the Seim River in Glushkovo was destroyed in a series of ATACMS strikes, Now, Russian reinforcements from a huge area in Kursk region are essentially cut off. Reportedly, 700 Russian soldiers are left stranded with no supplies The area under control of the Ukrainian armed forces keeps growing daily. It’s expected to continue. With the destruction of the bridge, the whole south-western part of Kursk region (over 50 settlements) is cut off from the rest of Russia. The Ukrainian forces are now targeting another of bridge in the village of Zvannoye, one of the 2 smaller bridges that are still operational. If all bridges are destroyed, further 700km² would fall under Ukraine’s control, in addition to the 1,100km² already controlled by Ukraine. If Ukraine keeps blowing up bridges and seizing territories west of the river, the Ukrainian Armed Forces will control 3-4 thousand square kilometers, full of with underground bunkers and storages, build by Russians as fortifications. In early 1990s, the KGB seized a similar territory in Moldova and established so-called Transnistria Republic. Russia still controls this territory and uses it to create problems for Moldova. Meanwhile, some Russian propagandists warn that squeezing out the Ukrainian forces from Kursk can “take months” — and other go as far as suggesting that Russia can lose this war. Ukraine’s Kursk offensive has blown a giant hole in the tale that “Russia is keeping its best forces in reserve”. No, they don’t: they are ”all in” in Ukraine — and are now trying to plug the hole with fresh conscripts serving compulsory 1-year service, unable to find any trained troops or “contractors” hired specifically for the Ukrainian war. Makes you think, right?

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why do you think the Russian government has refused to open a criminal investigation into the death of Alexei Navalny?
Answer: The Russian state officially announced they wouldn’t be investigating the death of oppositionist Alexei Navalny — naturally, the FSB doesn’t want anyone near the obvious murder case, implicating Putin’s regime. Apparently, Navalny became unwell during his morning walk. He complained of a sharp stomach pain. He was taken back to the solo punishment cell by the guards, where he was thrown for some “violation”. It was the 27th time Navalny was in a solo punishment cell, usually this would be a 14-day punishment. He was found unresponsive in his cell later by guards and taken to medical quarters, an ambulance was called, but couldn’t revive him. A day before his death Navalny participated in a video hearing of his complaint and was in good spirits, appearing healthy. 2 days before his death, his parents visited him in prison, and also reported he was feeling well. The details on the actual circumstances of Navalny’s death were apparently reported by some guards or other prisoners through connections that his friend, investigator Christo Grozev, and other anti-Putin Russians in exile have within the Russian prison system. The papers provided by the Russian investigative committee, refusing to investigate causes of death, say that Navalny was taken to the medics from the walk. The official document also doesn’t mention Navalny’s complaint about the sharp stomach pain. Death was recorded at 2:17 pm. The time of death was recorded at that time, which is already fake, as he had likely died in the cell — he was unconscious when taken to the medical quarters. ”He was dying alone,” said Navalny’s widow Yulia. The cause of death is listed as “the combination of several illnesses”, and the main cause as “arrhythmia” (which is unidentifiable posthumously and never previously was diagnosed). Looks like Navalny might have been poisoned by an unknown toxin. Which probably will be never found, because the family agreed to bury the body. It’s 6 months since the death of Alexei Navalny. The team of investigators, linked to his exiled colleagues, still didn’t post anything conclusive about the causes of his death, but it’s possible they know much more than what his widow Yulia Navalnaya revealed in her yesterday’s video. It’s possible they even know the names of those FSB officers who visited the prison at the time, tasked to kill Navalny.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What are some positive aspects of Russian culture and its people?
Answer: Russian military correspondents are furious: residents of Kursk region are evacuating, instead of queuing to sign up as volunteers for the Russian army. (Video in the comments below.) “What the heck??” barks a Russian man dressed in a military uniform. “As males, you should be defending your homes, you should be delivering food to our guys, or digging trenches — or if you can’t do it, just give your cars to our guys, so they can use them at the front. Why are you just driving away??” For 25 years, since Putin took helm in Russia, the state was training citizens to be passive: “They at the top know best what to do”, “we are just small people”, “we can’t change anything”. People have learned to don’t have any opinions of their own, because having an opinion can get you in trouble. They’ve learned to “stay out of politics”, learned to live by the motto, “my hut is at the edge of the village, I don’t know anything”. Putin’s administration chose to downplay “the situation in Kursk region” and Russian propagandists are now saying that “Ukraine made a foolish move” and “everything is under control, situation stabilized, no losses.” Kursk residents know it’s not true — they can look out of the window and see what happens, but because the state tells them “it’s all good”, they simply do what they feel is the right thing for them — run away. They don’t want to defend Putin’s regime, they don’t want to fight and possibly die defending their homeland. It’s weird, but there are no public protests in Russian towns taken over by the Ukrainian forces, as there were in spring 2022 when the Russian army invaded Ukrainian cities and thousands of Ukrainians went to town squares to protest against the Russian invaders — Ukrainian men, women, elders, kids were standing with bare hands against armed Russian soldiers, yelling at them, “Go home!!” “Occupiers, go home!” — protests in Kherson in March 2022. Similar mass protests were happening in many other Ukrainian towns captured by the Russian army. People in Kherson were standing with Ukrainian flags, with anti-Putin and anti-Russia posters, against armed Russians and military vehicles. Russians don’t protest. They seem to be indifferent to what is happening around them. They realized their officials lie to them — they knew it all along, but it was safer to pretend they believed them — and they have no idea what is real and what is not anymore, they just don’t trust anybody — but pretend to trust the guys who are in charge right now. If Ukrainians are in charge, they pretend to trust Ukrainians. If Russians are in charge, they pretend to trust Russians. Russian citizens have no opinions of their own — or if they do, they keep them buried so deep, they themselves are terrified to admit they have them. It’s not a “slave mentality” — it’s learned helplessness. They really think there is nothing they can do that will change anything. Obviously, this aspect of the modern Russian culture and collective psyche is highly beneficial to the advancing Ukrainian army, which doesn’t have to deal with hostile population. Rather, Ukrainians are dealing with passive, yet quietly curious population, compliant and eager to follow instructions. Russian State Duma member Vitaly Milonov called on men from the Kursk region to sign contracts with the Ministry of Defense and defend their homeland on their own — obviously, Putin isn’t going to send to Kursk reinforcements from the front in Ukraine, where he’s sending most troops and equipment. Milonov, too, believes that only women, children and the elderly should be evacuating from Kursk, but local men should take on the defense of border areas. “No one has to do anything for Russian residents of border regions,” announced Milonov — they themselves must show that they can defend their land. With such an attitude from the Russian state, no wonder that Ukrainians keep taking over several more settlements every day. Isn’t it weird that Russians are willing to go to Ukraine “to make Russia great again” (and be paid “big wages”) — but have no desire or interest to defend their own homes?

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How can the USA get rid of Russian agents in the USA?
Answer: Meet Dimitri Simes — a frequent guest of Russian TV shows, introduced as an “American political scientist.” This week, the FBI raided Simes’ estate in Huntley (Rappahannock County, Virginia). According to Simes’ neighbors, on August 13, FBI agents came to the estate and removed items from there. They came again on the following day. The Simes purchased the 130-acre Virginia estate for USD $1.63 million in 2021. According to journalists of Rappahannock News who talked to Simes, he stated that he was out of the country and no one notified him of the search warrant. Moscow-born Dimitri Simes is the publisher of “The National Interest” magazine and former president (1994-2022) of the American Center for the National Interest. 76-year-old Simes was once an unofficial adviser on foreign policy to president Nixon and traveled with him to Russia and the countries of the former USSR. The Telegraph described Simes as “an ethnic Russian US citizen who has become a cheerleader for the Kremlin.” Simes’ mother was a lawyer for Soviet dissidents, expelled from the USSR by the KGB in 1977 — while Simes immigrated in 1973, aged 24. The family settled in the USA and Dimitri became a naturalized U.S. citizen. Simes’ involvement with Putin’s regime seems a bit too tight for a former foreign policy advisor to a USA president. Given Putin’s open proclamation of the war on the “rules-based world order” and Russia’s drive to destroy the West, the FBI can legitimately suspect Simes of being an undeclared foreign agent. I really hope the likes of Jackson Hinkle and Scott Ritter could be properly investigated for their links to Putin’s regime. As well as other Putin’s shills in the USA.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What are the optics in the Kremlin as a result of Ukraine's audacious incursion/invasion?
Answer: TAP ON THE PHOTO TO VIEW. Putin was looking more twitchy than usual during the latest conference where “the situation in Kursk” was discussed. (Video in the comments below.) The regional governor and other Kursk officials made their reports, and while listening to them, Putin rubbed hands, constantly looked at his notes and kept glancing around. Maybe it has something to do with medicines he’s on. Or the stress is getting to him. ‘The Spectator’ expressed their own understanding of the situation. The Kremlin gang is in despair. They didn’t expect such a move.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is Ukraine delivering humanitarian help including food to the Russian citizens in the town of Sudzha? Is it true that the Russian Air Force is dropping bombs on the homes of Sudzha's residents? Will Russian forces bomb their towns in Kursk region?
Answer: TAP ON PHOTO TO VIEW. The Ukrainian forces are distributing humanitarian aid — food, water — to the residents of Sudzha, a town in the Kursk region that had been cleared from the Russian army.. Meanwhile, Russian pilots are dropping bombs on Sudzha, because Putin ordered to “squeeze the enemy out” — but the only way that Russians know how to fight is to turn everything into ruins, and then send stormtroopers to take over the ruins. The Russian state doesn’t care about the civilians who are still there — the city administration left first, and the police forces surrendered. Previously, Russia in the same fashion bombed the towns in Belgorod region, during incursions of the Russian Volunteer Corps into Russia in 2023. Ukrainian military administration in Sudzha, headed by general Moskalev (not a misprint) offers evacuation to residents in both directions — to Russia and Ukraine. Those who want to get out of town, can get out of town. The residents say they were abandoned by the Russian state — there was no evacuation, only these who could get out on their own cars were able to leave. Ukraine doesn’t plan to occupy the territory of Russia. The Ukrainian incursion into Russia is purely defensive, insisted Mykhailo Podolyak, advisor to the office of the President of Ukraine. “In the border regions of Russia, including Kursk region, Ukrainians deal exclusively with security-related tasks,” stated Podolyak. “Ukraine is not interested in occupying these territories. But it is interested in the actual destruction of many Russian military facilities, pushing the remnants of Russian troops beyond the lines that allow for artillery and ballistic missile strikes on Ukrainian territory, forming a security belt around Ukraine's borders, and destroying military logistics and infrastructure (including storage bases, training centers, and places where equipment is concentrated),” explained the Podolyak. He pointed out that Ukraine and Russia are “waging different wars.” “While Russia deliberately attacked Ukraine to kill civilians and occupy its territory, which is an unconditional war crime, Ukraine is waging an exclusively defensive war, including on the aggressor's territory to ensure the protection of its own population, which is its unconditional right,” stated Podolyak. Since the beginning of the offensive in the Kursk region, the Ukrainian Armed Forces have captured already 82 settlements, the territory of 1,150 km² and 35 km in depth, reported the commander-in-chief of the Ukrainian Armed Forces Syrsky. Russia can end the war any time — they just need to withdraw troops from Ukraine. This option remains available to the Russian state, but it doesn’t look like Putin’s government intends to make any steps in this direction. Instead, Putin’s army is turning border towns of the Kursk region into ruins.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why is Russia such a rich country?
Answer: “Cash payments from 5,200,000 ruble for the 1st year” are advertised on Moscow billboards, as the flow of volunteers willing to die for Putin’s ambition of conquering Ukraine had dwindled. A few days ago Muscovites reported that billboards and commercials advertising army contract service, promoting “A real job for men” and “Join your mates” suddenly disappeared from streets and subway TV screens. Now we know what was the reason: the Russian government decided to quit half-hearted attempts to appeal to citizens’ patriotic feelings and concentrate on the only thing that seems to work — offering “breathtaking riches” to those who are willing to kill Ukrainians. For your reference, 5,2 million ruble is about USD 58,000 — a monthly wage of $4,833, for 12 months. This includes a one-off payout on signing the contract (in Moscow it’s ₽2,3 million), and monthly wages of ₽215,000. That’s the known payouts, although they don’t make ₽5.2 million, but the keyword here is “from” — some other payouts like a yearly bonus after 12 months could be included in the number, advertised on billboards. The big problem is, a Russian combat soldier isn’t likely to survive for a year on the Ukrainian front. Most of the “army contractors” attracted by “big money” end up dead within 2–3 months at the front line, with many not returning from their 1st assault. Since the beginning of the war in Ukraine, one-off payouts have been increased manifold — because a number stops looking attractive to risk one’s life. 2 years ago, when posters were calling to “Join your mates”, payments were much smaller. Muscovites are especially unaffected by such promises — so the contractors who sign up in Moscow are mostly impoverished residents of other regions. They arrive to Moscow, get registered in a dormitory with a temporary Moscow address (it’s done by companies that get paid ₽50,000 for each willing conscript), and then sent to the front as “Muscovites”. Putin doesn’t mind, as long as on paper it looks like Moscow is just like all other poor regions of Russia, sending its young men to die in Ukraine. For comparison, the median monthly wage in Russia in 2024 is approximately 50,000 ruble (USD 560), according to Rosstat numbers (Russia’s state statistics body Rosstat uses many manipulations to make numbers look better: for instance, only taking into account wages of companies with 10+ personnel). But even if we believe Rosstat, the monthly wages offered to the “cannon fodder for Ukraine” are more than 4 times higher — and if we take in consideration the upfront payout spread over 12 months, 10 times higher. In impoverished Russian regions, even 50,000 ruble monthly wage is a good one — and 10 times more sounds astounding! Poverty in Russia’s regions is shocking. And you only need to drive 100 km from Moscow to see it. The ”volunteers” come from villages with no asphalt roads, from wooden huts built 100 years ago. It is in these poverty-stricken villages that the Russian “volunteers” that signed army contracts, hoping to pay off their debts, are finally buried. For decades, Moscow has been pulling all the money from the sales of its resources into the capital — with some cash also going to a few more large cities — while the rest of the country was decaying further. Foreigners arriving to Moscow and St. Petersburg (Russia’s “second capital” and the home town of Russia’s dictator Vladimir Putin) are easily deceived by the shiny gloss of these cities — but that’s the gloss of the Capitol in “Hunger Games”. Russia as a country may be resources-rich, but the vast majority of Russian people are poor.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Will Russia break up?
Answer: In the light of recent events, old maps depicting Russia are being updated. Ukraine is now establishing military administration offices in the Kursk region. Their goal will be humanitarian aid to the local population — many older people were unable to evacuate, or decided not to leave because they have livestock or animals. These civilians now struggle without food or water. The remaining residents are getting food parcels to survive. Ukraine also offers to help them to evacuate to either Russia or Ukraine, as they wish, and will offer humanitarian corridors in both directions. Ukrainians helping old people in the Kursk region, who were left behind. There is an opinion that as the result of the war unleashed by Russia against Ukraine, the Russian Federation will break up. This happened with the Russian empire after WW1 and with the Soviet Union after the war in Afghanistan. As the result of the war in Ukraine, the territory of the Russian Federation might also shrink. If there is even a state called “the Russian Federation” at the end. Some say, more than a few federal subjects of Russia — Dagestan, Chechnya, Tatarstan, Bashkortostan, Buryatia, and more — will want out.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How strong is the Justice Department's case against Kim Dotcom?
Answer: 50-year-old Putin lover Kim Dotcom will be extradited to the United States from New Zealand on criminal charges relating to the defunct file-sharing website ‘Megaupload.’ German-born Dotcom, who self-identifies as an "internet freedom fighter", has been fighting extradition to the US since 2012, following a raid on his Auckland mansion, requested by the FBI. NZ Justice Minister Paul Goldsmith has signed an extradition order for the German-born Internet grifter today. Took 12 years, but finally! Dotcom is accused in Conspiracy to commit Racketeering, Conspiracy to commit Money Laundering, and Criminal Copyright Infringement, and faces a maximum of 20 to 55 years in prison if found guilty. In response to the order, Dotcom verbally abused the country that was his home for the last 12 years, calling it an “obedient US colony in the South Pacific", and announced he’s going to fight the extradition order. The US authorities allege that Dotcom’s “Megaupload” cost film studios and record companies over $US500 million by storing and sharing copyrighted material, while generating whopping $US175 million in revenue for Dotcom’s “venture”. 3 other company executives were accused of intellectual piracy with Dotcom for “Megaupload”: 2 of them entered plea deals in NZ last year, and one died in 2022. A Putin lover in hot waters — that’s always a beautiful sight! Hopefully, the NZ authorities took care to confiscate Dotcom’s passport, so he can’t skip the country to seek shelter in Russia. Waiting for Maria Zakharova to complain about the lack of freedom of speech and democracy in the West.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Will tanks become obsolete with the rise of drones and missiles?
Answer: Ukraine is now using 30 robot dogs from the UK with German thermal camouflage in combat in Donetsk region. Robots are directed by the operator, they search buildings or Russian trenches. The robodogs are another addition to the army of aerial and naval drones successfully used by the Ukrainian defenders against the Russian army, which is struggling to keep up with warfare innovations. Tanks are expensive and their life on the modern battlefield is very short. Armored personnel carriers are more in demand and remain useful, as people still need to move around, to take positions. The problem of modern tanks is their thin armor at the top, which makes them vulnerable to drone attacks. But if the tanks are reinforced at the top, this would improve their survival on the battlefield, making them able to withstand both drone and missile hits. The next generation of tanks might become a mighty force once again.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why do Russian soldiers always prepare to blow themselves up when there is no hope to get out alive?
Answer: A young Russian soldier tried to blow himself up, because their commanders told them not to surrender to Ukrainian forces. He survived to tell his story. (Video in the comments below.) The Russian commanders tell their soldiers that it’s better for them to blow themselves up with a grenade if they are being surrendered — because otherwise, commanders threatened, they would be horribly tortured. This young man and his mate decided to follow their commanders’ advice — but luckily for them, they weren’t successful and only got wounded. The Ukrainians who captured them brought the Russian medic, part of the same unit, who was also captured, to attend to the wounds properly. Then they transported the wounded captives to a hospital. It’s been known for a while that Russian soldiers are advised to blow themselves up in case they are about to be captured. Some soldiers even do it when they are being attacked by a drone. The issue with this isn’t only the certain loss of life, but also the soldiers who do it are not eligible for the 5 million ruble ($56,000) death payout. If the self-blow recorded on video, the family will be denied the payout, because it’s considered self-harm, and not a death in combat. Still, the commanders keep telling scary lies to their soldiers (they don’t tell them about cancelled death payouts). Probably, because they fear that otherwise soldiers will be surrendering en masse. Mass surrender is what’s been happening in the Kursk region since the Ukrainians invaded. Videos where the Russian soldiers mass-surrender are all over the social networks, with new videos popping up daily. One explanation of that: Kursk region had a large number of Kadyrov’s guys (“Akmat” units) stationed there “to guard the border”. They are known for their cruelty to Russian soldiers from non-Akhmat units, with rapes of young Russian conscripts being a “norm” that’s accepted and not even worth complaining about. Russian soldiers may be more terrified to be shot by Kadyrov’s guys for not wanting to fight (“Akhmat” is also used as “barrier troops” that shoot deserters) than by their prospects at the Ukrainian captivity. Fear is how Putin’s goons rule.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Could I buy cheap apartment in Ukraine in their new city, Kursk?
Answer: The Ukrainian forces haven’t reached the Kursk city as yet — and probably don’t have such a goal. But they have already achieved multiple strategic goals. For the first time during this war, the combat is happening on the territory of Russia on a large scale. Previous raids into the Russian territory by the Russian volunteer corps (made of Russian citizens) that fight on the side of Ukraine didn’t last long and weren’t as deep. This time it’s a proper large-scale military operation with the use of heavy equipment and thousands of troops. Roman Sheremeta, professor of economics at Case Western Reserve University, points out the results that Ukraine had managed to achieve by its Kursk operation: And the added bonus for Ukraine is that now the fighting is on the Russian soil and any devastation will be Russia’s problem.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: In Russia, did the video of the effeminate Russian soldiers surrendering to the manly Ukraine army make them embarrassed?
Answer: TAP ON PHOTO TO VIEW. Young Russian conscripts saved by the Ukrainian army from certain death — Putin’s goons sent them to fight hardened Ukrainian fighters, but the kids were so scared, they surrendered. Russia has a 1-year compulsory military service that ever male must go through at the age of 18. Those who study at universities get to finish their studies first, before they are drafted. So, if you have graduated from the high school and didn’t get into college, you are immediately drafted into the army. Compulsory draftees aren’t supposed to be used in combat in the war, but you know, it’s Russia. The Russian generals decided it’s time to send everyone they have to the slaughter, to stop the Ukrainian incursion in the Kursk region — and another one, rumored to soon be incursion in the Belgorod region. In St. Petersburg, about 500 “refuseniks” were sent to the Kursk region. They included sick, mentally unwell, old, and “peaceniks”. Some of the captured Russian conscripts even tried to blow themselves up with a grenade — but failed, because of lack of experience. They say that the commanders brainwash them to blow themselves up to avoid being taken captive — the commanders tells them that otherwise, they would face incredible torture in the Ukrainian captivity. (Video in the comments below.) The unsuccessful grenade blower (who was hurt but not gravely) was shocked at how kindly he was treated by the Ukrainians — better than by their own commanders. These testimonies will be certainly of interest to the Human Rights commission of the UN and prosecutors of the Russian war crimes. The number and quality of those captured by the Ukrainian army in the Kursk region is so great (even some Kadyrov guys were taken captive, although Kadyrovets are given the order not to surrender — so they usually run away in case of any danger), that Russians even asked for a prisoner swap — apparently, for the first time during the war. This was reported by Ukrainian Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets. But if you were watching the Russian TV, you’d never hear about 2,000 Russians soldiers taken captive within 8 days — according to the Russian TV, things are going great in the Kursk region, Ukrainians are being defeated, “the situation has been stabilized”, and Russia is victorious, as always. As the war has been progressing through the last 2.5 years, Russians are getting more and more victorious — and the victories are happening closer and closer to Moscow. We soon might hear about new Russian victories in Belgorod and Bryansk regions.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is it confirmed in Russia that mass long range Badger strike, have targeted Russia’s Voronezh, Kursk, Savasleyka and Borisoglebsk air bases up to 500 miles over the border, and has hit Moscow’s ability to use Su 34s for glide bomb attacks?
Answer: The Russians posted videos recording sounds of explosions and subsequent fires in social networks hours before the Ukrainians confirmed a massive strike at 4 Russian military airfields at once. The Russians claimed to have downed over 117 drones, but the damage is undeniable. The drone attack was a joint operation between the SBU, AirForce, Special Forces, UAV Center of Ukrainian Armed Forces the Defense intelligence. Ukrainian drones struck 4 airfields in Voronezh, Kursk, and Nizhny Novgorod regions of Russia. The military airfields "Khalino", "Savasleyka", "Borysoglebsk" and "Baltimore" were targeted. These airfields host Su-34 fighter-bombers, Su-35 fighters and other military aircraft. The strike targeted warehouses with fuel and munitions, including supersonic “Kinzhal” missiles, located at the airfields. If reserves of T-6 kerosene were destroyed in the drone attack, it means the bombers won’t be able to launch supersonic "Kinzhal" missiles. On top of that, Ukrainians shot down a Russian Su-34 fighter jet over the Kursk region overnight. Roads leading to airfields under attack were blocked for civilian traffic. This was the biggest attack on Russian airfields since the start of the war.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Where are Russian Kursk reinforcements coming from?
Answer: Reportedly, Russia is scrubbing for soldiers and pulling anyone, to send them to Kursk, where the Ukrainian army invaded on August 6, 2024. Troops are transferred to the Kursk region from Kaliningrad — which is actually the area surrounded by NATO countries. Shows you how much Putin is really worried about “NATO aggression” — he’s leaving all other areas near border bare, to throw soldiers into the Ukrainian meat grinder. Some troops and heavy equipment are also being transferred from the Kharkiv region of Ukraine, where the Russian army tried to advance. 500 Russians who refused the military service on the base of “conscience objection” and health issues were grabbed in St. Petersburg region and flown to Kursk. Some of them have mental health issues. “They took a man with category “D” [unfit for service], plus a man of about 70 years old who could barely walk, and another man without an eye…”, a relative of one of the soldiers said. By the morning of August 13, about 150 people were delivered to a military training ground near Kursk. Another 300 “refuseniks” were taken in another direction. Several soldiers with minor concussions were taken away from the hospital in Kursk the day before. According to the witness, "everyone understands" that the soldiers are being taken somewhere near the border to fight in battles again. Conscripts in the Kursk region are being forced to sign contracts with the army, mothers of two draftees reported. According to them, there are currently about 150 conscripts in one of the military units in the Kursk region who are to be sent to the front as contract soldiers. (Conscripts who serve the compulsory 1-year service aren’t supposed to be in combat.) The conscripts are told that they would be "cleaning the area after the stormtroopers" and promised payments of 4,500 ruble per day (about USD $50). According to one of the mothers, her son was told: "You will go there anyway, but now [if you sign the contract], we will pay you the combat fee… And if you do not agree, then you will be sent to the military court — and still have to go to fight, you won’t have any choice." $50 per day for a most certain death within days. Life of Putin’s soldiers isn’t worth much. Same story is reported from the Murmansk region: conscripts are being prepped to be sent to Kursk. This includes young conscripts who were drafted last month. This is why the Russian soldiers keep surrendering to Ukrainians en masse. In less than 24 hours, another 100 Russian conscripts surrendered in the Kursk region, reported commander Syrskyi. Hitler, who started the World War 2, was responsible for the deaths of 14-year-olds who were sent to defend besieged Berlin in 1945. Putin, who started this war, will be responsible for the deaths of conscripts who are now being sent to defend the Kursk region. And many of them are already dead. Not everyone manages to surrender.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What role did the European Union play in the collapse of the Soviet Union, besides economic factors?
Answer: The Maastricht Treaty that laid down the foundation for the European Union was signed in 1992 and went into effect in 1993. The Belovezha Accords that resulted in dissolution of the Soviet Union were signed in 1991. The desire of the first Russia’s president Boris Yeltsin to take full control of the whole of Russia, without having to report to the Union state and the USSR president Gorbachev, was the main driver of that move. 3 presidents — of Belarus, Russia and Ukraine — signed the Belovezha accords on December 8, 1991. They actually were supposed to negotiate a new Confederation deal between the republics, to reenergize the Soviet Union, but the 3 presidents chose to destroy it instead. The European Union had nothing to do with it. It was pure greed and lust for power of the first elected leader of Russia.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What can we learn from the region around Kursk, scene of a famous Soviet counter-offensive in 1943, to understand the scale of the disaster inflicted on Russia by Vladimir Putin?
Answer: Russia-Ukraine war is full of symbols. Startling success of Ukraine’s offensive in the Kursk region — the scene of 1943 milestone battle of the WW2, where the Soviet army trashed Nazi troops — is one of such omens. Some western speakers make an obtuse mistake when talking about “Russia defeating Hitler” in WW2 — it wasn’t Russia but the Soviet Union. To understand the difference, bear in mind that when the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, more Soviet citizens were living outside Russia, than in Russia itself. By the same token, the Soviet effort against Nazi troops in WW2 also included more non-Russians than Russians. The second largest republic of the USSR was Ukraine — which was nearly fully occupied by Hitler in WW2, so the 7 millions Ukrainians in the Soviet Army really fought for the right to return to their homes. 1943 Battle of Kursk was the largest tank battle in history. It involved 6,000 tanks, 2,000,000 troops, and 4,000 aircraft. The USSR had 3,600 tanks, which was only made possible because of massive material support from the USA and UK. Without the American ‘Lend Lease’, the Soviet army wouldn’t be able to function at the level it needed to be. The Kursk battle dealt a final blow to German forces on the eastern front and decisively turned the tide of World War 2. Hitler troops lost the initiative, which they have never regained. So, the Kursk battle in WW2 was a turning point when the Nazis lost so badly, they never managed to recover. Soviets were proud of the Kursk battle (“Kursk Curve” in the Soviet history books). But for Vladimir Putin, the word “Kursk” is anything but pleasant. On August 12, 2000, Russian submarine “Kursk” sank, with Putin’s government screwing up the rescue effort, and all survivors aboard ending up dead. The people were especially shocked by the fact that Putin refused to return from his Black Sea vacation as the catastrophe was unfolding. On August 12, 2024, as the Ukrainian offensive in the Kursk region was progressing, president Zelenskyy said: ”We see how Russia really moves in the times of Putin: 24 years ago, there was the Kursk disaster – the symbolic beginning of his rule; and now we can see what the end for him is. And that is Kursk as well.” For superstitious Putin, the 2nd Kursk disaster must be petrifying — Putin certainly didn’t look confident at the latest briefing of Russia’s Security Council. For a long time, Putin was bragging about “Russia’s victory against Hitler”, completely denying credit to the allies (the U.S., UK, and others) and the input of other Soviet republics, including Ukraine. This time, Ukraine, backed by its allies (the U.S., UK, and others) is standing against fascist Russia — and the battlefield is once again in Kursk. This moment, no doubt, will be one of the focal points of the Russia-Ukraine war in future history books.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Will the liberated by the Ukrainian Forces Russian City of Sudzha become the new capital of the Russian Republic, also called Russia? Will it be similar to Taiwan vs communist-hijacked mainland China? Will Russia remove Kremlin reps from the UN?
Answer: By now, already 74 settlements are under control of the Ukrainian forces in the Kursk region, confirmed president Zelenskyy today. One of these settlements is the town of Sudzha, population 5,000, which is a district centre within the Kursk region of Russia. Sudzha is located 105 kilometers southwest of Kursk, the administrative center of the region. Surprisingly, Sudzha used to be the capital of the Soviet Ukraine! It happened over 100 years ago, during the Civil War. 1918 map of Ukraine. When Putin created an abscess in Donetsk and Luhansk regions in 2014, by sending Russian troops on tanks to capture territory, the story he was giving to the world was that it was a “spontaneous uprising of the people wanting independence from Ukraine.” No amount of Ukraine’s pointing it was an attack by Russia seemed to convince the world leaders that “the uprising” was Russia’s special operation to destabilize Ukraine. No one came to Ukraine’s help to kick out Russians out of Ukraine. The European leaders chose to freeze the conflict and convinced Ukraine to sign “Minsk agreements”, based on “accepting the situation on the ground” — but it didn’t bring peace to Ukraine. 2015, “Minsk-2” signing: Alexander Lukashenko (Belarus), Vladimir Putin (Russia), Angela Merkel (Germany), Francois Hollande (France), Petro Poroshenko (Ukraine). When Putin unleashed the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, world experts gave Ukraine just days (or weeks) until it would fall. Ukrainians surprised everyone — including Putin and his FSB goons — and managed to repel the Russian troops from Kyiv. It was only after Ukrainians pushed Russians from the capital and sank “Moskva” ship that the West agreed to assist Ukraine with weapons. By August 1, 2024 — 2.5 years into the war — many western opinion-makers were leaning towards the idea that the war in Ukraine reached a stalemate, and it was time for Ukrainians to negotiate with Russia. That Ukraine had no options but to cease fire and accept “the realities on the ground.” And Ukrainians managed to surprise the world once again — by invading Russia and taking over Russian territory. On August 6, Ukrainian army crossed into the territory of Russia, and on August 7, a Ukrainian flag was raised over Sudzha. History doesn’t repeat itself, but it rhymes. There is more than meets the eye, in Ukraine’s August 2024 operation. It may be more than mere coincidence that “traditional Ukrainian lands” are falling under control of the Ukrainian troops in the Kursk and Belgorod regions. As you remember, Putin’s main point of claiming the right to Ukrainian territories is that these used to be “historical Russian lands.” Zelenskyy shows that Ukraine, too, can play this game. Maybe they will even create a temporary government in the occupied Russian regions — the Ukrainian president already mentioned the need to provide “humanitarian relief” to civilians on the territories controlled by the Ukrainian forces. The situation is getting more complex and the simplest resolution for both Russia and Ukraine returning to their internationally recognized borders, as per mutually ratified Border Treaty of 2003, is likely to start gaining more supporters. “Despite the difficult and intense battles, our forces continue to advance in the Kursk region, and our state’s “exchange fund” is growing,” stated president Zelenskyy in his August 13 update. How fitting would it be if it were Russia begging to restore 1991 borders. “Preparations for our next steps continue,” ended his post president Zelenskyy. I’m sure we’ll see more unexpected developments in the coming weeks. Stay tuned.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What are some significantly awesome 'Meanwhile in Russia' photos?
Answer: New monument to Prigozhin and Utkin, killed by Putin, is looking ominous as the 2 figures look over innumerable black pyramids — tombstones to dead ‘Wagner’ fighters whom they sent to die for Putin. This is a metaphor for the whole of today’s Russia. Meanwhile in the Kursk region, the number of the Russian soldiers who surrendered to the Ukrainian forces have reached 2,000. Entire Russian units are refusing to fight. They just put their hands up and ask to be taken prisoner. A way better choice than turning into a little black pyramid. If you are lucky of course and your commander reports you dead — or you may end up as “missing” or an unidentified body in an overfilled morgue. Right now, there are so many Russian soldiers dying in Kursk region that there is a backlog on identifying corpses at the military morgue in Rostov. Bodies of Russian soldiers that were killed on August 7 are yet to be identified from 6 days ago. Because of maxing out on capacity, bodies from Kursk are no longer being taken to Rostov. Russian channels insist that Ukrainians are already retreating. Judging by the maps, towards Moscow.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How many towns and villages have Ukraine liberated in Kursk?
Answer: Vladimir Putin was furious about the governor of the Kursk region stating that Ukraine controls 28 settlements, and the zone that Ukrainians control is 12 km deep and 40 km wide, during a public live stream of Russia’s Security Council meeting. (Video in the comments below.) “Leave the numbers to the military,” barked Putin. From the start of the Ukrainian incursion into the Kursk region on August 6, the Kremlin tried to downplay the huge issue that the Russian army was facing in trying to defend its territory. Putin and Co. obviously hoped that this incursion was just a raid like the ones taken in 2023 by anti-Putin “Russian Volunteer Corps” (made of Russian citizens who fight on the side of Ukraine) — the units would enter the territory of Russia in small groups, take over a village or 2, make photos for PR, and then quickly retreat. This is why when the Ukrainian troops invaded the Kursk region on August 6, a decision was made in the Kremlin to treat it as another annoying but harmless “provocation”. That decision was a huge mistake, which Putin and his generals are surely regretting by now — because Ukraine brought across the border thousands of troops, including sabotage groups with Russian documents, who by now crossed further into Russia. Putin must be terrified of what the Ukrainians might be really planning. Shoigu and Gerasimov didn’t look particularly upbeat at the meeting with Putin — especially Shoigu looked like a dead man sitting. Which, according to many sources, he probably is. Most of Shoigu’s former deputies are fired or arrested on charges of major theft and corruption, and 2 of them have already “suddenly died”. The Kursk operation began soon after Ukraine got its first F-16s, which it has already been successfully using — a week ago, loaded Russian bombers had to turn around without firing the cruise missiles into Ukraine, obviously because the missiles would be shot down by F-16s, so the commanders decided not to waste the precious cruise missiles (Russia can produce only a few of them per month and they are exorbitantly expensive) — and rather return to base, to plan the attack differently. Also yesterday, Ukraine’s President Zelenskyy and his Commander in Chief Syrskyi (who participated in the briefing via a video link) for the first time provided an official information to the public on the operation in the Kursk region. Syrskyi announced that Ukraine now controls and occupies around 1,000 square kilometers of Russian territory — which is double the area that the governor of the Kursk region admitted. It’s worth noting that previously the newly appointed Russia’s minister of defence Andrei Belousov stated that Russia captured 850 square kilometers of the Ukrainian territory in 2024. As we know, these Russian advances in Ukraine came at the cost of over 200,000 personnel in losses (killed, maimed, and missing). Ukraine managed to capture a larger territory in Russia in just a week — with losses nowhere close to that number (Russia claims that Ukraine lost over 1,000 men in the Kursk offensive, but this is likely an exaggerated figure). Meanwhile, DeepState reports that not 28, but about 44 Russian settlements are already under the control of Ukraine, and the status of another 10 is unknown. The watchful viewers noticed the notes that Putin used to read his speech: The handwritten notes have giant letters — Putin is obviously scared to do a laser correction on his eyes, and doesn’t want to wear glasses or lenses. According to Moscow Times, Ukrainian troops advanced already by nearly 30 km into the Kursk region and begun to strike at bridges. But Putin’s generals insist that they have managed to “stabilize the situation”. The 26th year of Putin’s “stability” started really well.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What implications does the state of emergency in Kursk Oblast have on the region and its residents?
Answer: That’s not Ukraine — that’s Kursk region of Russia. After a recent incursion by the Ukrainian troops, there are already 180,000 Russian refugees fleeing from the fights in Kursk and Belgorod regions, bordering Ukraine. There is a new buzzword in Russia, “voluntary evacuation”. Instead of extending “the zone of SMO” (special military operation) on Kursk, Belgorod and Bryansk region, Putin announced a “state of emergency of the federal level” in these 3 regions and designated them as a “zone of a counter-terrorist operation” (CTO). 72-year-old Alexander Bortnikov, who is the head of the FSB, is appointed as the chief of CTO. This means a lot, first of all, for residents of the Kursk region. “CTO” was the name that Russia’s war in Chechnya was called from 1999 until it ended. When Putin was made the head of the state in August 1999, he was a nobody for general public. Until then, Putin only had background roles in administration and zero public image. To create a strong public image that would allow Yeltsin’s “successor” to become an elected president of Russia, Putin needed to quickly — within months — become a household name. The method that Putin’s clique selected was ghastly but markedly effective: The FSB began blowing up high-rise residential buildings at nights — Moscow, Buynaksk, Volgodonsk — prompting the reaction of horror and helplessness among Russian city dwellers. The new head of state showed up, promised to deal with the culprits (Chechen terrorists had been blamed) — and announced the 2nd Chechen War. The horrors moved from the territory of Russia to the territory of distant Chechnya, and muscovites breathed a sigh of relief. The Russian citizens were content with the Russian army destroying Chechen towns and villages, killing Chechens, so that they could sleep peacefully in their apartments. Vladimir Putin, who was constantly on TV screens giving instructions and making promises, instantly became a household name — and then easily won elections in March 2000. When Putin doesn’t know what to do, he falls back on what’s known and what worked in the past. Since Putin doesn’t know what to do in the Kursk region — his generals failed to prevent and contain the invasion by the Ukrainian forces — he’s going back to his “bag of known tricks”. This means that the residents of Kursk can expect what Chechnya went through, as well as what post-2014 Donbas had to go through. That's what the chief of FSB Bortnikov has been appointed for. That’s why the FSB was put in charge of the army in the Kursk region, and not the other way around. Putin’s factory of lies already began spreading fakes. The Russian propaganda is posting made-up stories about alleged crimes committed by the Ukrainian military against civilians of the Kursk region. For now, there is no evidence to confirm their accusations — but Ukrainians from Donbas know how the “proofs” are made up. Residents of the Kursk region need to be seriously wary when they see around some Russian military personnel or journalists. In Donbas, residents quickly picked up that wherever a Russian media crew shows up, it means civilians are going to be shelled — and the crew is sent there to film it. The residents of the Kursk region could become the next group who realizes who was “bombing Donbas for 8 years”. Other types of provocations are not off limits for the FSB: in Donbas, members of ‘Rusich’ brigade, backed by Russia, would change into Ukrainian uniforms and then abuse and shoot locals. Some were purposefully let go to tell the story that the settlement was “attacked by the Ukrainians”. It’s best for locals to evacuate into a safe zone — even though it’s more than likely that their homes will be looted or destroyed. There is simply no good option when the war came to your area — you have to choose between ‘bad’ and ‘very bad’. But because Russians have failed to make good choices, they are now left with choosing between ‘bad’ and ‘very bad’.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is Putin winning the global chess game?
Answer: When you started a global chess game and found yourself 2 moves from a checkmate. Putin’s administration released a bizarre video of Vladimir-the-Loser, shot against a green screen, promoting military exhibition “Army 2024”, bragging about “unique Russian weapons”. (The exhibition itself will be held in ”Patriot” park, whose management was arrested last week for theft and fraud — and almost the entire leadership of Russia’s Ministry of Defense is accused of corruption and embezzlement on an especially large scale.) In his bland speech, read from a teleprompter, Putin tried to revivify ideas of a “more just, multipolar world” and called international partners to “work together to create equal, indivisible security.” A great proposition from the leader of a state, which started the largest war in Europe since 1945 — and brought death, destruction and suffering not only to its neighbors, but also to his own land and his own people. “Our intention to build constructive cooperation is in demand and finds sincere, lively response,” said the leader of the state that threatens to send the world into nuclear Apocalypses nearly every week. The leader of the state that has been trying to subdue a country 35 times smaller in size for over 10 years — and is now being invaded by that country. The leader of the state that’s been losing hundreds of men every day on the battlefield for 2.5 years — killed, maimed and captured. The state, soldiers of which are now surrendering by hundreds daily, unwilling to defend their own land — and preferring to be locked in prison at the enemy territory instead. But in Putin’s own world, he’s still winning in the global chess game he started.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How did Putin handle the Kursk submarine disaster?
Answer: Relatives of the ‘Kursk’ submarine crew at the place where it sank in the Barents Sea. 24 years ago, on August 12, 2000, Russian nuclear submarine ‘Kursk’ sank after a torpedo on board exploded in its hatch, causing 2 massive explosions on board. The explosions were so powerful that they got picked by seismographs across the globe. The nearby 28,000-ton battlecruiser ‘Pyotr Velikiy’ shook from the 1st explosion. However, the Russian Navy didn’t acknowledge they had a major catastrophe. All 118 crew members aboard ‘Kursk’ perished, although 23 sailors survived the explosions and were alive for hours, hoping to be rescued. One of the ship’s officers, Lieutenant Captain Dmitri Koselnikov, left a note dated 2 hours after the 2nd explosion, saying there were 23 survivors. The submarine sank to the sea floor. The survivors barricaded themselves in a rear compartment and waited for a rescue. The rescue never came. ”Kursk”, a movie based on the disaster, starring Colin Firth, came out in 2018. As the disaster was unfolding, Vladimir Putin, the newly inaugurated president of Russia, continued his holidays on the Black Sea. Putin’s first statement about the submarine disaster was only made a week after. It took a week before a permission was granted to foreign countries to attempt a recovery mission (the Russian Navy failed to get into the sunk submarine) — and on August 21, a team of British and Norwegian divers accessed the vessel and found its entire crew dead. In 2000, the Russian media was still privately owned, so the coverage of how the Russian state handled the ‘Kursk’ disaster was sharply critical. Putin was furious over the ways TV amplified his haphazard response. He accused the TV producers in “hiring $10 whores” to pose as wives of deceased sailors, with the goal to portray him, Vladimir Putin, in a bad light. Kursk’s commanding officer, Gennady Lyachin; photo from 1999 parade. When questioned by relatives of the deceased on August 22, 2000, Putin put the blame on Russia’s “economic and military decline” before he came to power. It’s unlikely that there will be many mentions of the sunk ‘Kursk’ in the Russian media today. Not when Russia just suffered such a humiliating invasion by Ukraine last week, precisely in the Kursk region.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why was Russia's counterattack weak in the face of Ukraine's offensive in Kursk?
Answer: TAP ON THE PHOTO TO VIEW. Photo of the day: captured Russian conscripts are kneeling in front of a Ukrainian soldier. Russians in the border regions — both the troops and the civilians — aren’t resisting, because Russian citizens are trained to be passive. They don’t do anything without a command from the above, and once the Ukrainians shut down communications in an area, the Russians are staying idle, without their superiors yelling at them to motivate. By August 12, over 1,000 Russian soldiers have already surrendered to the Ukrainian troops in the Kursk region — the captives also include units of Russia’s FSB. The number of Russian captives starts posing a logistical problem for advancing Ukrainian troops: the captives need to be transported, fed, guarded. (Video in the comments below.) When Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, unarmed Ukrainians were standing against tanks and soldiers with machine guns. Now, civilians in Russia don’t even attempt to resist. But it doesn’t mean there is no fighting in the Kursk region. The situation in Kursk hospitals and morgues is critical — too many bodies and wounded. "They are transporting the wounded in batches, the killed in batches, all the cars and KamAZ trucks are filled with corpses and "300s" without limbs. When a truck drives in, blood just flows out of it,” locals report. Commander-in-Chief of the Ukrainian Armed Forces Syrsky posted a photo in which he is looking at the situation on the battlefield, accompanied by the words, “Continuing the operation." One thing that the Ukrainians are now saying, with a muted smirk, “We haven’t even started yet.” And that’s what Russians are really afraid of.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How likely is it that Ukraine has secretly prepared dirty bombs with nuclear material as a last line of defence against the Russian nuclear attack?
Answer: Every time the questions about “dirty bombs” pop up on Quora, it coincides with the intel on Russia’s discussing the covert use of tactical nukes in their fight against Ukraine. The Russian propagandists openly talked about nuking Ukrainian troops on the territory of Russia, following the Ukrainian incursion into the Kursk region. What is happening in Kursk is so embarrassing that Russian propagandists couldn’t help bragging about Russia’s nuclear prowess. And the idea of Russia’s nuking its own territory isn’t new either — Margarita Simonyan, the chief editor of ‘Russia Today’ propaganda center, talked about it already in October 2023, explaining that Russia has full right to blow a nuke in the air over the Russian territory. Meanwhile, this is reportedly a warehouse of Russian nuclear warheads. This rotten garbage is more likely to explode at the first touch than to fly anywhere. That’s more likely to act as a “dirty bomb.” And apparently, Russia is full of such warehouses — especially the European regions near the border. This is what everyone — especially Russians — should be worried about, and not some mythical “dirty bomb” made by Ukrainians.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How might the international community respond to the events in Kursk Oblast?
Answer: Tatyana Moskalkova, Russia’s human rights ombudsman (human rights in Putin’s Russia!), called on the UN to "condemn terrorism on the part of Ukraine amid the advance of the Ukrainian Armed Forces in Kursk Oblast." Because it’s the 6th day of the Ukrainian incursion into the Kursk region, and no one in the world really cares. Everyone is watching Paris Olympics. Putin also invaded Crimea in 2014 during Sochi Winter Olympics. And he was going to invade Ukraine in February 2022 during Bejing Olympics — apparently, only the personal request by Chairman Xi convinced Putin to wait until the Games ended. The Ukrainian attack also coincided with the 25th anniversary of Putin in power — it was on August 9, 1999, that the first president of Russia Boris Yeltsin appointed Putin as his “successor.” Coming back to Ukraine’s incursion into the Kursk region, I’ve been waiting for calls from the known Putin’s shills to “stop the futile resistance” and “be brave enough to raise the white flag”, addressed to the Russian army. After all, in just 5 days, the Ukrainian army took more territory in the Kursk region than the Russian troops managed to capture in the whole year in Avdiivka direction. The silence with which world players reacted to Ukraine’s surprise advance into Russia is astounding. And the most indicative thing is that Putin, instead of his usual threats and nuclear blackmail, was busy signing some laws (Putin signed record 115 laws on August 8), as if this were his main occupation, calling the Kursk incursion a "situation" — the hallmark of a strong leader, no doubt. And there is much more hidden in this silence than in all the loud statements and threats that we all have heard before.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Do many Russians believe Russia is its own continent?
Answer: “Russia’s borders don’t end anywhere” stated Vladimir Putin, meaning that “Russia’s interests” go beyond internationally recognized state boundaries. For decades, the state called “Russian Federation” was invading the lands of its neighbors at whim, often after purposefully creating unrest in border regions — and then invading “to fix” the problems. This modus operandi was used already in Stalin’s times and probably was taught in the KGB school, which is the alma mater of many Russian officials who came as part of Putin’s team, when Yeltsin’s daughter and her husband decided to install a former security officer as the head of state, in exchange to guarantees of personal safety for the Yeltsin’s “Family”. The anti-democratic coup didn’t happen when Putin went for the third presidential term in 2012 — not even when he appointed his proxy Medvedev as the president in 2008. The anti-democratic coup happened when Putin was officially appointed by Yeltsin as his “successor” 25 years ago, in August 1999. It was under Boris Yeltsin that Russia invaded Moldova in 1992 and started the First Chechen War in 1994. Under Putin, the idea of “Russia’s greatness” and the slogan of “The Russian world from Lisbon to Vladivostok” crystallized. This is now the aspiration that Putin promotes to his underlings, after giving them permission to plunder the raided territories — the rightful privilege of the conqueror, in their model of the world. According to the founding paradigm of “The Russian World”, Russia is “a separate civilization” — separate from both the West and the East. This paradigm is now the foundation of Russia’s official doctrine of international relations. Putin is as much a promoter of Russian imperialistic chauvinism as he is its product. After the crash of Putin’s regime, Russia will have a long way to go, to even have a hope at healing. And any healer would need to deal with the cause, not the symptoms.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why didn't Putin introduce SVO on the territory of Bryansk, Kursk, and Belgorod regions?
Answer: After the incursion of the Ukrainian troops into the Kursk region of Russia, Vladimir Putin announced “the state of emergency” in 3 border regions (Kursk, Belgorod and Bryansk) — but he didn’t include them into the “zone of SMO” (“special military operation”, as he calls Russia’s invasion of Ukraine). Instead, Putin announced the operations in the border regions a “CTO” — “counter terrorist operation”. The distinction is material: a CTO is managed by Putin’s enforcers of choice — the FSB, as opposed to the Russian army under the command of the Ministry of Defence. For instance, border patrol in Russia is also a division of the FSB. Russia doesn’t have enough forces in the Kursk region (and neither does the FSB), so Kadyrov’s commander Apti Alautdinov called on Russians to “join the final battle with the satanic forces”. (Video in the comments below.) Alautdinov’s units ran off from any fights with the Ukrainian forces on the border, where they were located, and Alautdinov explained that simply “Ukrainians walked pass them”, insisting that “nothing special had happened”. This was 3 days ago. Now Alautdinov calls on Russians to fight the Ukrainians in Kursk (under “Akhmat” brand) — Kadyrov is saving his trained forces to be able to defend his kingdom of Chechnya when Putin’s regime collapses, he has no desire to send his loyal Chechens to die for Putin. It shows that Putin doesn’t want to pull forces from Donbas, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson to fight off the incursion in the Kursk region (the logistics of moving them is also complex), and still hopes that the invasion of the Russian territory can be somehow stopped by only the forces that the FSB can find within Russia. But the desperate plea by Alautdinov demonstrates they don’t have enough forces. Interesting.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What do Russians think about Putin's wartime policies?
Answer: Dmitry Grinchiy was born in the infamous year 1937 — the year of Stalin’s ‘Great Purge’. Just a few months after little Dmitry was born, his father Pavel Grinchiy was arrested by the NKVD. In 1938, Pavel Grinchiy was shot as ‘the enemy of the people.’ Just like a million of other Soviet citizens were shot. At the time, the Soviet people zealously supported the fight against "enemies of the people." Stalin’s propagandists repeated every day that “enemies and spies are everywhere”, and that “we must remain vigilant.” And the Soviet people were vigilant. They wrote millions of reports to the NKVD, pointing out potential “enemies of the people”. In all probabilities, Pavel Grinchiy was shot because someone he knew reported on him. 87 years have passed. Dmitry Grinchiy (who never even got to know his own father, killed on Stalin’s orders), lived his life in the USSR — through the collapse of the USSR, through “terrible 1990s” and the 25 years of Putin’s regime, from its inception to the fated launch of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. In 2024, he found himself in a country where the regime every day tells the citizens that “enemies and spies are everywhere” and that “we must be vigilant”. And the Russian people are vigilant. Yesterday, 2 such vigilant Russian citizens attacked Dmitry Grinchiy on a bus in Moscow, they beat him up and dragged him to a police station. (Video in the comments below.) The 2 vigilantes decided that Grinchiy was “an enemy of the people” simply because (in their view) Grinchy said something “disrespectful” about the monument to “Wagner” — the chief of which, Yevgeny Prigozhin, was, by the way, killed on Putin’s orders after an attempt of armed rebellion. Some say that the recent incursion by the Ukrainian forces may lead to another “Justice March” towards Moscow. Fortunately for Grinchiy, the police decided to release him. Maybe because they didn’t want to lock up the old man immediately — the Russian prosecution machine has a habit of charging and locking up people after some time, even though initially the accused have been released after being detained and questioned. It’s unlikely the vigilantes will get as much as a slap in the wrist, after beating the old man. I’m shocked how quickly — in front of my eyes — Russia turned from a country pretending to be a semi-liberal democracy into a full-blown militaristic dictatorship, where people write reports on friends and family for “saying wrong things”, where books are being burned, with non-stop hateful propaganda from every screen. I’m shocked — but the majority of Russians are earnestly embracing “the new realities” with vigor and dedication not seen since 1937.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What do you think will happen after Vladimir Putin hears the report from his colleagues on what is happening in Kursk Oblast?
Answer: Rumors are, the days of Russia’s Chief of General Staff Valery Gerasimov are numbered. Gerasimov survived the recent purge in the Ministry of Defence, when the Minister Sergey Shoigu was demoted and several of his deputies arrested, with at least 2 of top level thieves in uniform already dead. But after a recent blunder of the Russian army in the Kursk region, where the Ukrainian forces entered through the border and invaded the Russian territory, with the Russian troops completely unprepared for the massive attack, the personnel of the General Staff saw the writing on the wall. Reportedly, the employees are cleaning their desks and quietly taking out things from their offices in backpacks and suitcases, preparing for the inevitable moment when a few uniformed men enter and give them 15 minutes to pack. During the incursion in the Kursk region, the Ukrainian Armed Forces managed to break through 2 lines of fortifications that Russia’s ministry of defence had built over 2.5 years of war, at the cost of 15 billion ruble. According to Bloomberg, Putin had not been informed about the potential Ukrainian offensive in the Kursk region, although the Russian intelligence knew about the buildup of the Ukrainian forces on the border 2 weeks ago. When attacked, the Russian forces were taken by surprise and offered no resistance. For 2.5 years, Putin refused to replace Gerasimov as the Chief of General Staff, despite the lack of strategic successes. It looks like Gerasmov’s luck have just ran out.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What do you think of the statement by Vladimir Putin that the events in Kursk Oblast were a "provocation" by Ukraine?
Answer: Putin already upgraded his definition of events in the Kursk region of Russia from “a provocation” to “a situation”. The Ukrainian side remains tight-lipped on “the situation” in Kursk, while the Russian media tries to downplay the breakthrough at the border by the Ukrainian troops. Every evening Russian propagandists report that “the Ukrainian troops have been destroyed” — and the next morning we find out that the Ukrainians have moved forward another 10–15 km and took several more settlements. What the Russian military correspondents have reported: Russian oppositional media gives a slightly different map, where already 700 square km are under control of the Ukrainian Armed Forces. One notable point about the Ukrainian operation in the Kursk region is that the local population is completely passive. When Russian tanks invaded the Ukrainian soil in February 2022, locals threw Molotov cocktails at them and burned them, tried to stop tanks with bare hands by simply standing in front, people blocked the Russian military equipment and went to rallies with Ukrainian flags. But there is no resistance from the Russian local population. In the town of Sudzha, the Ukrainian forces surrounded the police station and the cops simply put their hands up without resisting. Ukrainians took their weapons away and let them go. The ones who wanted to leave the town were allowed to leave for Kursk. This morning, the news came that the border in the Belgorod region has also been broken through by the Ukrainian troops that took over a village in 3 km from the border. Bryansk region is next.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Can Ukraine make its own weapons?
Answer: Ukraine can and does make its own weapons: Russia-Ukraine war of 2022–2024 is the first war in history where drones became the weapons that dominate the terrain. Within the last 2 years, drone production in Ukraine grew 100-fold. Since February 2022, Ukraine created and developed the UAV market from the ground up. One of such manufacturers are making drones called “Hornets”. There are smaller and larger FPV drones — “Wild Hornets”, “Queen Hornets”, as well as other models. All of them are Ukrainian-made. The Ukrainian drone operators have learned to use the same drone for many missions — a drone drops explosives and returns to the base, to get munitions.
