French president Macron said in his speech, “I thank the Ukrainian people for their bravery, and fight for freedom. We are with you. And we will not falter,” to the applauds of the audience. So, Putin’s Russia has been officially counted out of the alliance that won the WWII. 2024 Russia is a tyranny, and has no place at a memorial service where the values of democracy, freedom and equality are celebrated. And just to confirm it, Dmitry Medvedev posted on X (in English) that Russia intends to provide Russian weapons to “all those who consider the Yankeeland & Co their enemy, regardless of their political outlook and international recognition”, i.e. openly stated that Putin’s regime would be sending Russian weapons to illegal militarized groups, to use them against Americans. “Their enemy is the U.S., and that means, to us they are friends,” italized Medvedev at the end of his post for emphasis. That’s why Russia wasn’t invited to the 80-year anniversary celebrations of D-day. Because Putin’s Russia is a mafia-led tyranny, members of which are unwelcome in places that stand for freedom.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What is happening in Russia? Once again, Putin threatens to use nuclear weapons. Does this barking never end? Is Putin a gnarly little person with no self-confidence and that this is the reason for his threatening behavior?
Answer: Yesterday, Vladimir Putin gathered journalists of international media — which he rarely does in Russia after February 2022. This reflects the depth of crisis in the Kremlin, following the announcements of the USA and other western countries that Ukraine can now use the weapons they supplied to hit military targets on the territory of Russia. Not only journalists of “friendly” news agencies from Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, China, Iran and Turkey were invited, but also the media outlets from “unfriendly” countries — Germany, Japan, Spain, France, USA, Britain, and Italy. The western media stopped paying attention to Putin’s speeches, so he invited them to meet him in person, hoping this would make an impact. I think it did. Just not the impact Putin hoped for. The “bunker granddad” totally lost it. After answering questions for 3 hours (Putin rumbles — that’s why it takes so long), Putin became agitated, banged on the table and shouted that the West was as stupid as this table if they believed that Russia was threatening them. And before that, he threatened that Russia will send weapons to the countries or regimes that would hit the USA and Europe. Sounds looney for us, but for Putin, cognitive dissonance is his natural state of mind. About Putin’s threats, there is nothing new. That was 2 years and 3 months ago. Putin used his highest level threat — strategic nukes — almost immediately. And he keeps repeating it, over and over. And we all are just supposed to give in and give him what he wants. That was Putin’s plan — and he doesn’t have another one. Follow me for more updates!

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why do you think NATO's assessment is that Russian leader Vladimir Putin will try to delay the announcement of the next wave of mobilization?
Answer: Fresh units of the Russian army shipped to Ukraine look like this. Vladimir Putin is trying to delay the next wave of mobilization, hoping that either Ukrainians or the West will give up. Putin’s recruiters are working overtime promising Russian citizenship and salaries of over $2000 per month to young males from poor Asian and African countries, paying recruiters high premiums for selling out their countrymen. There are fighters from Cuba, Nepal, India, Syria, Mali, Sudan, and other African countries delivered to the front lines in Ukraine and sent in “meat attacks”. With the ongoing war, the next wave of mobilization in Russia is inevitable, but Putin is trying hard to postpone it. Obviously, a new wave of mobilization in major cities will expose the actual numbers of Russian casualties. Casualties in rural Russia are somewhat hidden due to the vastness of Russian territory, but in cities like Moscow and St. Petersburg the losses are visible to everyone. Putin already gathered and sent to meat assaults the least privileged and most gullible Russians, tempted by “big money”, who made a mistake to volunteer for his “special military operation”. The remaining men in Russia are better informed, and this is why Putin’s recruitment drive is now struggling. The new wave of mobilized, who would be more aware of the situation than those who obediently showed up to enlistment offices in September 2022, could rebel and turn the weapons against these who send them into meat attacks. Another issue for Putin is ideological. The fact that Russia still has the ability to mobilize gives Russians a glimpse of hope that not all is lost, since the Kremlin still has an ace up its sleeve. Once Putin announces a new mobilization and it doesn't change anything on the battlefield, reality will sink in and Russians will have no excuse that "we haven't even started yet." This is why Vladimir Putin is doing everything possible to delay another mass mobilization. That’s why there are constant raids on migrants, that’s why Putin pays premiums to foreign recruiters. The Ministry of Defense increased salaries for fighters. More African and Nepalese mercenaries, who don’t speak any Russian, are appearing at the front. Newly arrested criminals are offered to go to war instead of waiting for a trial. But these resources are finite. Especially considering how the Russian generals use them. In May 2024, deserters and soldiers who refused to return to the war after rehabilitation had been detained and forcibly sent to the front — instead of prosecuting them in due order. Soldiers with injuries were also not discharged but shipped back to trenches. The order to send them to the front came from the Kremlin. This indicates that the Kremlin is running out of the human resource and soon will have no other option to continue the war as to begin mass mobilization.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How does Russia use social media as a strategy?
Answer: In an interview on Russian TV, Margarita Simonyan confessed that “Russia Today” is creating 1000’s of fake accounts, to spread disinformation. (Video in the comments below.) In February 2023, in the interview with Boris Korchevnikov for his program “Life and Destiny”, editor-in-chief of ‘RT’ spilled the beans about something, which, in Simonyan’s own admission, she “shouldn’t be talking about”: “It’s best for me not to talk about it… But I will say it bluntly: we create a large number of informational sources, which are not linked to us. And while the CIA investigates and uncovers that they are linked to us, they already have a giant audience. Sometimes they uncover that, shut them down. Sometimes, you wake up in the morning and 600 of your channels have been shut down. But while they are shutting them down, we have already created new ones. So, we are in this race, running after each other. It’s even fun,” Simonyan smirked. “Russia Today” is just one Russian propaganda outlet that uses social media as a strategy. They are oriented on foreigners. The fake accounts created by Russian propaganda outlets are supporting real media personalities, expressing pro-Putin views in the western informational space. I don’t even need to name the names here, we all know who they are. These personalities are paid by entities established by individuals linked to the Russian state and siphoning Russian money to them via a chain of offshore companies and funds. On the lowest level, coordinators from the Russian disinformation departments are hiring commentators from poor countries (including Russia, as well as countries of Asia and Africa), whose job are likes and dislikes, views, and comments under certain posts or accounts. These commentators are hired through online “tasks” websites and paid a few cents per “task”. To earn $10, the commentators likely need to “work” for several hours, but kids and elders with nothing to do are happy to get a few bucks without needing to get off the couch. Thus the poor quality of the majority of pro-Russia comments. There are dozens of such websites with digital tasks. In addition, automated bot accounts ran by software are used to artificially increase the number of likes and views. The Russian state is working very hard to defeat the West. And if Russia’s successes on the battlefield in Ukraine are highly questionable, the Russian propaganda is a mighty enemy that needs to be taken seriously. Just as seriously as the Russian bombs.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Will Putin drop a nuke just to get the world to stop laughing at him?
Answer: I keep hearing that “for Putin, it’s better 10 more years in a bunker (with a pool) as President and Commander in chief, than the alternatives (Gadaffi etc).” The problem with this idea: I’m still trying to figure out how Putin is going to survive in a bunker for 10 years. Just imagine it: a few hundred people, each of whom lost family members. Lost everything and everyone they had. Lost their freedom. On tight rations. Can’t go out. Limited circle of communication. Depression, mental health issues. And all of them know whom to blame for what happened to them and their loved ones. How long until there is a coup to depose the leader? I’d say, months, if not weeks. And that’s the scenario where Putin isn’t hunted down by NATO special forces, and the air supply to the bunker hasn’t been cut off. I just can’t see Putin starting a full-on nuclear war. (Many actually believe Russian nukes won’t work due to lack of maintenance over the last 33 years, and rampant corruption in the army — but that’s another story.) Putin would really, really like to drop a nuke. But only if he isn’t punished for that. If he knows he’d be a hunted criminal worldwide after that — like Bin Laden — that’s not what he’s trying to achieve. He’d rather take his chances with Russian people (who’s proven to be more docile than he imagined), and sell his loss in Ukraine as a “victory”. Russian propagandists have already prepped for that: So, if there is no more shelling of Russian cities, no more war, then Putin “won” a war against 55 countries — Russia is intact, “protected its sovereignty”, not split into 20 countries, all goes “back to normal”. And anyone trying to say that Russia hasn’t won, goes to jail. Putin remains the master strategist.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What are Russian nuclear threats to Europe?
Answer: Alco-General Andrey Gurulyov was assigned the job of voicing the latest nuclear threat to Europe on Solovyov’s TV live show. (Video in the comments below.) According to Gurulev, who is the chief of the Defence Committee in the Russian State Duma, Netherlands is a “fat target”, where a hit with a ballistic missile would produce the worst damage. “But it must be nuclear!” jumped in Solovyov, who realized that alco-Gurulyov forgot the most important part of the threat he was designated to verbalize. “Sure, sure, nuclear,” repeated Gurulyov after Solovyov. “This will put Europe on its knees.” ”We shouldn’t be afraid to talk about it!” ended his tirade Gurulyov. A year ago, Gurulyov had a different view. A year ago, he insisted that Britain “should be destroyed” first. “The first thing to do is sweep away Britain. Completely. Demolish it from the face of the Earth!” Gurulev demanded on Skabeeva’s show in March 2023. What a year can do to a person. Gurulyov looks a decade older now — I suppose, all top execs in Putin’s government struggle to sleep at nights, expecting a knock on the door. Recent arrests in the Ministry of Defence don’t add confidence in job security. No one paid attention to Putin’s mumbling in Tashkent last week, when he mentioned “highly populated European countries” that should be careful about supporting Ukraine. Putin had been banned from threatening nukes by Chairman Xi, who is adamant that nukes shouldn’t be used. So, now the orders were given by Putin’s AP (administration of the president) to the whole gang of Russian propagandists to push open threats mentioning “nukes”. The online Kremlin bots also became more active with, “Putin will throw a nuke if he doesn’t get his way”. Posts of known Kremlin bots are so awesome to see what’s actually the current sore point for Putin. As you know, for months before the invasion of Ukraine, Kremlin propagandists vehemently denied that Russia was going to invade. Now, the same propagandists insist that “Putin will throw a nuke, and it’s not a bluff!” If Putin was really going to throw a nuke, they would want to do it in secrecy — American ‘Patriots’ are able to shoot down the most sophisticated Russian missiles (including “hypersonic” Kinzhals). If the air defence units are on high alert, Putin has virtually zero chance that the missile will hit the intended target, but 100% chance of a mighty responding strike. So, if Putin were preparing to throw a nuke, they wouldn’t threaten it. Vice versus, the propagandists would be talking “peace” for weeks. As the arrests of Russian generals and various top executives are ongoing in Moscow, Putin’s position is extremely vulnerable in Russia. An army coup — or even an FSB coup — isn’t out of question. Getting to the anniversary of Prigozhin’s mutiny (23–24 June), Putin certainly isn’t in a position to give orders that completely change the status quo. There is Global Peace Summit in Switzerland on June 15–16, and delegates from over 90 countries are attending. Throwing a nuke would mean that the camp of those willing to support Putin will shrink to a dangerously low number. This, the current probability of Putin attempting to hit Europe with a nuclear weapon (and this includes Ukraine) is the lowest since February 2022, when Russia unleashed its full-scale invasion. And the reason for that is the strong and decisive response from the West and massive continuous assistance to Ukraine. Hitting back is the only language that Putin’s goons understand.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How badly has Putin damaged Russia?
Answer: The wives of mobilized soldiers kneeled in front of Russia’s ministry of defence, requesting to meet the new minister Belousov — they hoped to beg him into allowing their husbands to return home from Ukraine. “Please return daddy home,” “Belousov Andrey Removich, we exist, talk to us!” say the posters. What kind of mental state these women needed to be brought to, so that they kneel in front of the people who have screwed and robbed them all their lives, and now they are simply killing their children, brothers, husbands. “We want justice,” the women chanted when Colonel General Borisenko was sent to talk to them (the commotion was starting to gain traction online). 500,000 Russian soldiers have been mobilized and sent to Ukraine — it wasn’t their wish, they didn’t volunteer, didn’t sign a contract in hopes to earn “big money” — and only a dozen or so women demand to bring back their husbands. The ratio of caring russian wives protesting for the return of their husbands and the silent wives nowhere to be seen is astounding. Borisenko told the wives of mobilized that they were “rocking the boat” and had no right to be called citizens of the Russian Federation. He also confirmed that their husbands would be in Ukraine until the end of the war, because “55 countries are carrying aggression against the Russian Federation”. Poor “peace-loving” Russia, again struggling so much… Maybe, it’s time to withdraw its soldiers from foreign countries, if it’s in such dire straits?

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why was Scott Ritter's passport confiscated?
Answer: Yesterday, a former junior military analyst and sex offender Scott Ritter was forced off a plane heading to Russia, his passport confiscated by border patrol. Former judge Andrew Napolitano, who also intended to fly to Russia, was stopped with Ritter and was unable to travel, “on orders of the state”. Both of them were traveling to the annual St. Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF) as guest speakers. “I was boarding the flight. 3 officers pulled me aside. They took my passport. When asked why, they said ‘orders of the State Department’. They had no further information for me,” Ritter complained to ‘Russia Today’. “They pulled my bags off the plane, then escorted me out of the airport. They kept my passport,” Ritter said. Putin-lover Ritter was due to appear on the forum along with Judge Napolitana, Larry Johnson and Jackson Hinkle. Larry and Jackson left early and are already in Russia. In Moscow, Kremlin speaker Dmitry Peskov was unruffled about Ritter’s not being allowed to fly to Moscow. When asked about Ritter, Peskov responded that there was nothing unusual about a former intelligence officer facing travel restrictions. Peskov’s close friend, Shoigu’s deputy General Timur Ivanov (left) was recently arrested “for a bribe” (presumed treason), and is now locked in Moscow’s Lefortovo jail. At present, Russia doesn’t allow any former military or government employees out of the country, without a prior permit from the FSB (unless they are being shipped to fight in a foreign country – Ukraine, Syria, Niger, the list goes on).

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What should Russians stop doing immediately?
Answer: #1 thing that Russians should stop doing immediately is giving support to Putin’s war in Ukraine. The Kremlin is not protecting Russia from being attacked, but waging a criminal war of aggression — and Russia itself is now suffering from this war more and more. As soon as the war stops, the shelling of Russian regions will end. To bring this moment closer is the duty of every citizen of Russia. Russian troops must be withdrawn to Russian territory, and all war criminals must be brought to justice. Putin announced a fight against the West and NATO, and fought this war for so many years, that now it got to the point where NATO weapons are hitting military targets in Russia. What is this, if not a victory of a great geopolitician? Russian soldiers drafted to army to serve 1-year compulsory service are not supposed to be serving in the regions of hostile combat, but there are draftees in the Belgorod region. Draftees could be guarding air defense batteries, which are now being hit by western weapons. The risk of death for any Russian serviceman becomes higher and higher. Any Russian man who is in the army should understand that military service puts them in immediate mortal danger, whether they are arriving to the conscription office as potential draftees or think about signing up for a contract service. Putin will die, the war will end, but the lives and health lost are unrecoverable.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Are Russians surprised that they didn't take Kyiv "in three days"?
Answer: There were countless statements by Russian propagandists that “taking Kyiv will only take 2–3 days”. Even Belarus leader Alexander Lukashenko made such a statement. In March 2022, Putin himself ensured Russians that “there will be no need for mobilization” — only to announce mobilization 6 months later. So, yes, Russians indeed were expecting that their troops will just march on Kyiv and have a parade in the afternoon. The coping strategy of Russian propagandists is to claim that: The current slogan on billboards in Russia, “Our victory is inevitable.” I’d like to see how Russian propagandists will explain it when Russia loses Crimea and Donbas. Probably, they will say that NATO tried to liquidate Russia as a state, but Russia managed to remain on the globe, and therefore it won.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is Russia becoming an Orwellian nightmare? It seems that time and time again Russian war supporters say the most fabricated, nonsensical, self contradictory, and blatantly hypocritical nonsense it's possible to say?
Answer: In a dilapidated building in Ivanovo, a town 300 km from Moscow, a “George Orwell library” has been functioning for 2 years. (Video in the comments below.) It was open by local businessman Dmitry Silin, who at the start of the war was personally handing free copies of “1984” to Russian people in the streets. Silin gave away over 600 copies of Orwell’s masterpiece. Journalist of ‘France 24’ TV channel Karina Chabour wanted to film a story about Silin’s giving away Orwell’s books, but on the very first day of filming, she was arrested by the Russian police. Her translator was also detained. The French journalist and her interpreter were released after the police recorded their “misdemeanor”, but she was unable to complete her plans for filming in Ivanovo. Later, Dmitry Silin was accused in “discrediting the army” — not for handing out the copies of Orwell’s dystopia, but for a scribble on the wall saying “No to war”. Silin denied he was the one who painted the graffiti, but in Russia you are guilty if the prosecution says you are guilty. In September 2022, Silin left Russia, to avoid criminal conviction. He said he was disappointed that he “couldn’t do anything for Russia.” “Freedom is the ability to say that 2 times 2 equals 4,” asserts the phrase on Silin’s T-shirt. Surprisingly, the “Orwell’s Library” founded by Silin was able to function for 2 years. The library showcased different editions of “1984” and other books by Orwell, as well as had sessions screening films that were banned in the USSR, offered lectures about overcoming the feeling of helplessness, discussions about books. The library gathered a collection of dystopias, books about Stalin’s GULAG, works of modern writers who are critical of the Kremlin, as well as old-time Soviet political manuals. None of these books had been banned in Russia, so offering them to public wasn’t illegal. “The more dystopias you read, the more freedom you have: they show you the dangers, how to avoid them, how to resist them,” believes 68-year-old library director Alexandra Karaseva. 41-year-old lawyer Anastasia Rudenko, co-founder of the library, said she could see the signs of the totalitarianism described in “1984”, in the modern-day Russia. In June 2023, Rudenko was prosecuted for “discrediting the army”. The offensive material was found in her posts on Telegram (she only had 400 followers there). Anastasia Rudenko with Dmitry Silin. In one of her posts Rudenko retold the dialogue from the Russian film “Nuremberg”, showcasing trials of Nazi war criminals in 1945: At the end of the publication, Rudenko wrote: “Listen to these words... does this remind you of anything?” For this and several other posts, Rudenko was found guilty in “discrediting the Russian army”, but only given a fine. Anastasia Rudenko. Now, the “George Orwell library” in Ivanovo, which she co-founded with Silin, has to close its doors — nothing sinister, the building is up for sale, and the library was requested to leave. The aged activists and volunteers intend to find another place and reopen it elsewhere. I’m thinking of the FSB. They are certainly watching the library and have a file on every activist. And while the activists think they are doing the right thing, they are actually teaching doublespeak to their visitors, teaching how to do pointless things that make no difference to defeating Putin’s regime and ending the war in Ukraine. I think, to be effective, anti-Putin Russians don’t need a library. They need something different. Entirely.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How can I motivate myself to quit smoking?
Answer: Ukrainians posted this photo: “Give up smoking, or you will pass away and won’t see how Putin meets his death.” That’s a new level of motivation!

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How do the latest numbers of attacks in Kharkiv Oblast compare to the previous ones?
Answer: “From 100 people in our regiment, only 10–12 left,” tells the Russian soldier about the attack in Kharkiv region that he was a part of. (Video in the comments below.) Russian soldier Anton Andreev from the 5th company of the 1009th regiment explained in a video that he recorded it in case he doesn’t make it out alive, to describe what really happened during the attack on Vovchansk, a small Ukrainian town 5 km from Russia-Ukraine border. “I don’t know whether I will get out of all this or not, but at least to honor the memory of those who died like meat here, because of certain individuals,” Andreev blurted bitterly. According to Andreev, who posted the video online, the operation to attack the Kharkiv region began earlier than planned. The soldiers were sent into attack by foot, in a bulletproof vest and with a gun in hands — nothing else. The fact that Russians are now sending infantry into battle in these rusty DIY meat buckets is probably the best illustration as to the catastrophic level of equipment depletion in the Russian army. Many Russian soldiers who were thrown into the attack had only 4–5 days of training. Most of them had been shot by machine gun fire, as they were trying to advance. Obviously, with no prior combat experience, they had no idea how to survive in a real battle. The commander of the unit was constantly yelling at them to go forward. The task was to advance and take street by street, but in 2 days, they could only get to the first “bastion” at the first street, and were unable to go move forward after that. One assault group after another was taken down by machine guns and FPV drones. A group wasn’t allowed to retreat until half of its soldiers were down, only after that the commanders would allow them to return to base. “You pass a street, everything seems to be fine, but then you get caught up in a massacre — under machine guns, especially drones — they take out so many personnel! And the command on the radio shouts, “forward, forward!” You cannot retreat. When there are 5-10 people left from all groups, maybe they'd let us retreat, but then it's already half of them are "300", [wounded] Andreev described the attacks on the streets of Vovchansk. Initially, Andreev’s company was told that they would serve as rear guards and also bring weapons to the front line. But instead, they were all thrown into battle. The same story we’ve head hundreds of times before from the Russian soldiers — promised a safe unit to serve, used as cannon fodder instead. During May 2024, daily losses of Russian troops increased to 1,500 people (wounded and killed). The Kremlin does not care how many lives of Russian soldiers are lost. And what was the point of the “offensive”? After 3 weeks of non-stop attacks, 70% of the town of Vovchansk is destroyed. Most of the destruction is due to Russia’s use of gliding bombs, which Russian pilots offload already over the territory of Russia, in Belgorod region. Turning Ukrainian towns into rubble is what Russians call, “liberation”. Russian propagandist and “military blogger” Alexander Kots reported that in the Kharkiv region, the progress of Russian troops had stalled: "The enemy does not have lack of shells anymore. They also operate a wide range of FPV's. There is a gradual fortification at the reached borders and we are slowly moving into active defense, because if we try to go further, we will simply lose a large number of our people. And we see that, judging by the behavior of the enemy, they are preparing a serious counter-offensive blow in the Kharkiv area." Russians are willing to sacrifice tens of thousands of their young men, to be able to destroy Ukrainian towns. Insane.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What will happen to economics in Russia?
Answer: “Always low prices” alcohol store a year ago, in June 2023, and now, in June 2024: that’s the price for cheap beer made in Belgium and Germany. Price rise of over 35%. Russian people, most of whom buy the cheapest available goods (regardless of the quality), struggle to purchase food and drinks they used to be able to afford. After mass-market foreign clothing brands like “H&M” left Russia, local clothing chains raised their prices by 50–100% — for the same quality clothing as they were selling before. The difference in prices “before the war” and now is staggering for residents of Rostov, who try to save not only on entertainment and clothing, or occasional coffees in a cafe, but also on basic essentials like purchasing store-made baby food — there is simply no money in a family budget left for that in a family of 3, with father’s solo income of 50,000 rub. per month ($500). In Russia, a monthly salary of USD $2000-3000 is considered “high” — only 3% of the population earn such money. People who earn $2,000 per month are viewed in Russia as “rich”. Russia is a poor country and the war will ruin it completely.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How can we bomb Moscow?
Answer: In theory, Finland has the capability to successfully bomb Moscow. Finnish JASSM-ER stealth missiles with nearly 1000km range could easily get the job done, since we know that Ukraine can fly non-stealth, slow drones for thousands of miles into the Russian territory. Of course, Finland, which joined NATO in April 2023, won’t be bombing Moscow, unless Russia attacks a NATO country (which Russian propagandists and Russian officials threaten to do every week). Putin threatened to attack “any country that helps Ukraine” already on the day he launched his full-scale invasion in February 2022. He began threatening nukes within days. That’s the highest level of escalation Russia is capable of, and Putin threw that highest level threat nearly immediately. In 2 years and 3 months, NATO gained 2 more member countries, and Russia gained additional 1,300 km border with the NATO. During this time, NATO countries updated their plans how to respond to various Russia’s military actions, now basing on the knowledge that Putin isn’t a rational actor and prone to making the most moronic choices. NATO has never been better prepared to promptly provide a mighty response to a Russian aggressive action against a member country. Even though Putin refuses to face the reality, most people surrounding him see the writing on the wall.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What does the average Russian citizen have to look forward to in the future?
Answer: More and more Russian men who are trying to leave Russia are being turned back by officers of the Russian border control. Tour operators complain that many of their tourists are stopped at the border and banned from leaving Russia, their international passports get confiscated and cancelled. The border control officers are using “incorrect spelling” as the reason to confiscate a passport (Russians use Cyrillic alphabet and names can be spelled various ways in Latin alphabet). Simultaneously, there are raids on city streets where men are being grabbed and brought to military enlistment offices, and then immediately taken to military units — disregarding any documentation about health problems etc. that would make the men unfit for military service. Russian troops suffered the most terrible losses in May 2024 since the start of the full-scale war in February 2022, because of the failed attempt at offensive in Kharkiv region. In just 1 month, the Russian troops lost almost as many soldiers as in 10 years of the war in Afghanistan. Opening another front in Kharkiv region has been an absolute disaster for Putin's army. The Russian troops are unable to compensate for the losses by the intake of “volunteers”, which is drying up, despite the higher one-time payments offered on signing the army contract: in Moscow and nearby regions, recruiters offer 1 million rub. on sign up ($10,000). The lack of volunteers makes the pressing need for another wave of mobilization even more urgent. Mind you, the hidden mobilization has never stopped — over 500,000 Russian men have been mobilized (as opposed to signing the contract voluntarily), while initially (in Sep. 2022) Putin was talking about mobilizing 300,000 men. So, all Russian men under 50 can look forward to potentially being grabbed by police, thrown into a bus and sent to Ukraine as cannon fodder. Those men aged under 60 can look forward to a likely lifting of the mobilization age. Women in Russia can look forward to buying protective gear, clothing and boots for their mobilized men, as often the gear provided by the army is of extremely poor quality, or no gear provided at all — recruits get hand-me-downs from wounded and dead at the front. Another development that all Russians can look forward to — mobile bomb shelters. Such shelters have already been installed in street of Belgorod, and residents use them during air raids. (It is from near Belgorod region that Russians shell Kharkiv, and this is where the counter battery fire hits back.) Now similar bomb shelters are going to be built in the streets of other cities. For over 2 years, Russians have been cheering the planes and missiles flying towards Ukraine. Now, they can look forward to Ukraine hitting back.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What is the general attitude of Russians towards Ukrainians? Are there many exceptions to this rule?
Answer: Russia is “waging a vile, unjust, terrible, bloody war”, says Anatoly Belyi, 51-year-old Russian actor who performed in the most famous Moscow theatre for 20 seasons. Belyi left Russia after the start of the full-scale war, because he saw that most Russians support (or don’t care about) Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. “Yes, I left. I left the theater and everything else. Guided by the concept of professional honor, I finished my 20th season at my beloved Moscow Art Theate, performing, gritting my teeth, so as not to damage the theater — and then left the country that was waging a vile, unjust, terrible, bloody war. I can’t pretend that nothing is happening, I can’t see people laughing in summer cafes, I can’t hear cheerful music flowing from open doors. I can't be silent anymore. My country was knocked off its feet, along with the people whom I considered friends (only a few remained), along with those for whom I performed on stage, naively believing that I was at least somehow influencing their souls and hearts. What a fool I was. I expressed my position at the beginning of the war both on the oppositional TV ‘Dozhd’ and in my social networks. There was so much evil and hatred in response that I realized that it was useless, indeed the majority of people are supporting it. And I went silent. I guess you could call me a defeatist. But I really think we lost this battle. By “we” I mean the culture, those who thought and hoped for the democratic development of our country. There are only a few of us. And we can be blown off the face of the earth and history very easily. Russia doesn't need us. It's a pity. Because there are a lot of wonderful people in Russia. Beautiful people. But there is more darkness. It’s a bitter truth, but it must be accepted. My main word in these dark times is ‘disappointment’. It’s very deep and multifaceted. Disappointment in human nature, in the victory of the bestial unconscious over the weak mind. Darkness rules. And I do not exalt myself, I am not a knight on a white horse. I leave my Egypt every day and a lot of things don’t work out. But I'm trying. I guess I'm one of those who are unable to laugh after Auschwitz. That tragedy is historically far away and we haven’t experienced it, but now it came into my life. It came unexpectedly and terrifyingly. And I still don’t know how to live with it. I am a pessimist and I think that the darkness that has come to Russian soil will last for a very long time. It will definitely last during my lifetime. This morning a rocket hit Vinnitsia. Adults and children died. I was born in Vinnytsia region. Since February 24, I have a huge stone inside me, it weights on my soul and my heart is in pain every day.” In December 2023, Russian authorities announced Anatoly Belyi “a foreign agent.” His real name is Anatoly Weissman, and he now lives in Israel. The pseudonym "Belyi" (it means “White” in Russian) is a translation of the German name "Weisman" into Russian. In 2024 Belyi narrated the Russian-language voiceover of the documentary film ‘Auschwitz’ produced by Steven Spielberg.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What is the current state of the Russian people?
Answer: 50-year-old Russian State Duma member Vitaly Milonov called for a ban on women going without underwear in public. That’s apparently something that is greatly disturbing for the state of mind of the Russian people, in the eyes of the Duma legislator. Meanwhile, Dmitry Medvedev, another prominent Russian political figure of comical proportions, is preoccupied with thoughts about American actor George Clooney. Yesterday, news came through that George Clooney’s foundation will be asking for arrest warrants for Russian propagandists, who all love visiting Europe. Today, the deputy chair of Russia’s Security Council Dmitry Medvedev threatened to send Russia’s “very attentive, highly trained professional journalists” after Clooney, “to have a chat ‘from dusk till dawn’” with him. I know a lot of people simply view Medvedev as a clown. But Medvedev is a deputy chairman of Russia’s Security Council and a former president of Russia — he’s a top Russian official, and that’s the level that top Russian officials are now functioning at. Pretty weird that Medvedev is suddenly worried about European arrest warrants against Russian propagandists. The patriots should be staying in their beloved Russia, shouldn’t they? Why bother visiting the evil and rotting West? Anna Neistat, director of legal affairs of the Clooney Foundation’s “Docket” project, explained that unlike the Russian military and their commanders, many Russian propagandists like to travel around Europe, have residence permits, family and property in different countries — and can be detained on the basis of a warrant in Europol member countries. In many European countries, “propaganda of war” is a criminal offense. This means, the Russian propagandists can be arrested in any European country and extradited to the country that is investigating a criminal case against them. Neistat said the warrants won’t be made public — those propagandists who call “to bomb Europe” should get a welcome surprise on landing. The news should make lives of Russian propagandists more exciting, I suppose. Imaging going on a trip, not knowing whether you’d come back or get handcuffed at an international airport. What a thrilling life!

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why are journalists being labeled 'foreign agents' in Russia?
Answer: The newest “foreign agent” in Russia — Maria Andreeva, whose husband is a Russian soldier fighting Ukrainians in Ukraine. The designation of Andreeva as a “foreign agent” actually makes sense: her husband makes big money fighting as a mercenary in a foreign country — Ukraine. Other people who got labeled by the Russian government as foreign agents — journalists, writers, bloggers, musicians, actors — often have no connection to foreign sources of income. But in Russia, funding is no longer the reason to be branded “a foreign agent”. It’s enough to “be influenced” by foreign ideology — things like democracy, human rights, dignity, compassion, historical facts. Anything that Putin’s regime sees as a threat to their narratives is labeled “discrediting the Russian army” or “discrediting authorities”, and anyone mentioning inconvenient ideas or facts (or reporting on people who mention the inconvenient ideas or facts, in case of journalists) are now “foreign agents”. In fact, such people are obliged to register as “foreign agents” voluntarily. There haven’t been arrests for failure to register as a foreign agent in Russia as yet, but give it a few months, we’ll surely see it. Being labeled as a “foreign agent” creates a lot of trouble for the individual. They can’t be elected officials or be involved in elections in any capacity, they must include a disclosure statement in capital letters in all their public posts (if they fail to do it, they are hit with big fines), their books are removed from libraries and book stores, they have to file special financial reporting. Along with Andreeva, who is an activist of “The Way Home” movement of wives of mobilized Russian soldiers, politician Yekaterina Duntsova was announced yesterday a “foreign agent”. Just a few days ago, Duntsova filed documents to register a political party. Instead of denying her application, the Russian government announced her a “foreign agent”. Problem solved. Meanwhile, kids of the chief of Russia’s Central Bank, Elvira Nabiullina, who managed to escape to Norway (the kids escaped, the mother is still in Russia working for Putin’s regime), officially became Norwegian citizens. Just as Putin is again threatening to nuke Norway and other European countries that help Ukraine. The first time he made this threat was 2 years and 3 months ago — in February 2022. I wonder, how Nabiullina — and other Russian officials — feel about Putin’s threats to turn their families living in Europe and the USA, into “radioactive dust”? They must be feeling very excited about fighting for the right to spend the next 10 years in an underground bunker with Putin and his concubines.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What is the likelihood of success of the protest by the wives of mobilized Russian soldiers?
Answer: Yesterday, the movement of wives of mobilized Russian soldiers was announced a “foreign agent.” Let the absurdity of it sink in: the families of Russian soldiers who are actually fighting in Ukraine with weapons in their hands, under artillery fire and missile hits, who obediently went to “defend the homeland” — whom Putin calls “the new Russian elite”, are branded “foreign agents”. How good is that? That’s a sensational success, in my books! All the wives of mobilized were doing was to complain about the lack of equipment at the front and demand to let their husbands come back home. They posted complaints on Telegram (where they have less than 60,000 followers), and once a week laid flowers at monuments to soldiers who died in WWII. The media even stopped reporting about them. And now, suddenly, these women (the participants are basically exclusively women) are branded “foreign agents” — and have to label themselves as such, under the threat of hefty fines. The first reaction from the wives of mobilized was “go f**k yourself!” (yes, for real). Then they continued: “After so many months of awkward threats and crap thrown at us in the media, the authorities have finally decided on their opinion about us. Now we too are agents of the reptiloids and enemies of the regime. I wonder if there will be evidence? Of course not. And ‘The Way Home’ has never been funded by anyone. Insanity and fear are getting stronger. What's next? Will mobilized and contract soldiers who complain about the lack of payments and uniforms become foreign agents? Foreign agents with weapons in their hands? Or maybe everyone except the members of ‘United Russia’ are foreign agents? The absurdity is gaining momentum. But we don't intend to stop. Our loved ones are still in mortal danger, under the rule of the "patriots" of Russia and friends of the state. Well, now we have entered the list of cultural representatives: actors, musicians, writers. Congratulations to us or what?” Well, ladies, congratulations!! You’ve earned the highest recognition — Putin’s regime officially views you as a threat.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Was socialism a failed experiment?
Answer: I lived in the socialist Soviet Union — and had a chance to see socialist Poland, Romania and China in 1989. I traveled around the republics of the Soviet Union in mid-1980s (all 15 USSR republics became independent countries in December 1991, when the Soviet Union was dissolved). And then I traveled to the countries outside of the socialist sphere — Greece and South Korea. Whenever I talk to these enamored by marxism, socialism and communism, they say that the socialism (communism) in the Soviet Union wasn’t the proper socialism (communism) as it should be. Neither it was obviously “the correct socialism” anywhere else. Because the communism (socialism) described by Marx is a utopia. It doesn’t exist. It’s like a perfect woman. Or a perfect man. They don’t exist because real things aren’t perfect. Soviet Union was a real attempt at building communism. It didn’t work, so they called it “socialism” and said communism will come next, when the socialism gets “fully developed”. They spent 70 years trying. It didn’t work — not for the lack of trying. And every attempt at building communism (socialism) was accompanied by mass murders. Whole classes of the society were “liquidated”. They needed to erase any memory of normal life, so life in the “socialist” (“communist”) state seemed normal. But it could only seem normal if you didn’t know anything different. This is why they were locking people inside the country, not allowing them out. Not even allowing them to see a different version of socialism. Because then people could have questions. Communism (socialism) means total control of the state over people. The adepts of socialism say there was state housing, and even though the food was very basic, people weren’t going hungry. But it’s the same in a prison — you have a small room to live in, you are being fed. Are there many people dreaming of being imprisoned? Strangely, there are a lot of people dreaming of socialism.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What does Putin hope to achieve with all of this, and how do you see it?
Answer: Putin hopes to achieve immortality and a place in history — and to achieve that, he is prepared to sacrifice people, money, friends, anything. To score a place in history, Putin chose the role of an anti-West crusader, who announced the collapse of America and European Union as his ultimate goal. Initially, Putin wanted to resurrect the Soviet Union. When he was unable to do it because the countries he wished to seize control over were leaning towards the West, Putin began blaming America in messing with his plans. Whatever he tried to do didn’t work out as he planned – and Putin was growing more and more frustrated; the idea of destroying America and the West became his dominant motivation. Putin became obsessed with the idea that to win the battle against America, he needed to seize control over Ukraine (based on musings of former USA National Security Advisor Zbigniew Brzezinski) — it became his “idea fix”. Ukraine is Putin’s Holy Grail. He genuinely believes that he who controls Ukraine, controls Europe — and holds the key to controlling the world. It may sound insane (because it is insane), but Putin is completely isolated from the rest of the world and only gets information as printouts in red folders, from a select group of advisors. Anyone who’s bringing bad news gets axed as a traitor. Putin’s second source of news is the Russian television. And the Russian television and its speakers get instruction manuals from the AP — presidential administration, which is the same closed circle of people who supply Putin with printouts in red folders. Putin watches Solovyov, Skabeeva, Symonyan and it makes him feel good about the situation. To understand how far Putin’s insanity had gone, you only need to look at yesterday’s award ceremony in Kremlin, with recipients making speeches that sounded like a competition in cajolery. The winner of that contest was, indisputably, Steven Seagal, who got awarded the Order of Friendship by Putin. If you didn’t know, Seagal is responsible for Russian–American friendship, and his profound successes are irrefutable — the relations of Russia and the U.S. hadn’t reached such a level in decades. Seagal’s speech (in English, because despite being a Russian citizen since 2016, Seagal can’t obviously speak Russian) was a compilation of the most ludicrous lies of Russian propaganda about Ukraine. (Video in the comments below.) The speech was most certainly written for Seagal by Putin’s administration, but because Steven can’t read Russian, he put it through an automatic translator and read the resulting gibberish from the screen of a mobile phone. “Cringeworthy” would be too kind a word to describe that happening. The speech of another award recipient, Stas Mikhailov (he identifies as a pop-singer), came close second in terms of cringeworthiness: “All power comes from God. God is with you. God blessed our country. God is with us. And if God is with us, who can be against us? We are with you. Victory will be ours!” Other awarded Putin’s loyalists — Duma Speaker Volodin, Senate Speaker Matvienko, Moscow mayor Sobyanin — gleefully cheered and clapped. These constant award ceremonies and celebrations certainly have the vibe of a ‘Feast in Time of Plague.’ So, how does Putin plan to achieve his goal? This was spelled out by devout Putin’s mouthpiece Margarita Simonyan: there will be an ultimatum, and the West will give in. That’s their plan. For real.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is Zelensky a legitimate president?
Answer: Under the Ukrainian law, Volodymyr Zelensky a legitimate president of Ukraine. Under the Ukrainian law, there shouldn’t be elections while the martial law is enacted in the country. The presidential elections should be held within months after the martial law is cancelled. During the last week, Vladimir Putin, who imprisoned or killed all his political opponents (the ones who didn’t emigrate), before refusing in registration Yekaterina Duntsova and Boris Nadezhdin as candidates in 2024 Russian presidential elections (both spoke in favor of ending the war in Ukraine) — this wannabe Russian “tsar”, who changed the constitution of Russia twice, to be able to stay in power for 25 years, was using any opportunity to make a speech questioning the Ukrainian President’s legitimacy. Russian propagandists have all been given an instruction manual to do the same. Diana Panchenko, who is a former Ukrainian journalist who ran to Russia (she was even given the opportunity to interview Belarus leader Alexander Lukashenko last year), launched a poll in her X account, asking whether her followers consider Volodymyr Zelensky a legitimate president of Ukraine. She got an unexpected result: Despite the huge number of bots under control of the Kremlin propaganda department, 91% of the poll participants voted “yes” in the simple 2-option poll, confirming they consider Zelensky a legitimate president of Ukraine. Over 2 days, more than 5,700 people cast their votes. Panchenko herself denies that she lives in Russia, saying that she resides in the United Arab Emirates — the destination where Putin-lovers prefer to hang out, while Moscow keeps repelling these pesky drone attacks. Despite not living in Ukraine, Panchenko keeps calling herself a “Ukrainian journalist”. Which is weird, because according to the Kremlin propaganda’s official line, “Ukraine doesn’t exist”. Putin’s propaganda is trying to stir a “discussion” about Zelensky’s “legitimacy”, but there is really nothing to talk about: Ukraine will announce presidential elections as soon as Russians withdraw their troops. If Putin wants to assist in any way, he can give an order to his commanders to bring the Russian soldiers back home. They certainly will be happy to return to their families alive.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How would the provision of Patriot air defence systems affect the situation in the city of Kharkiv?
Answer: More than 10% of the population of Kharkiv (160,000 people) have lost their homes, 5 thousand buildings suffered damages or have been destroyed by the Russian artillery, missiles and bombs. If Kharkiv had effective air defence systems like Patriots, with sufficient munitions for them, this wouldn’t have happened. The White House administration has finally approved the use of American air defence systems to shoot down Russian planes over the Russian territory — that’s where they drop their guided bombs, which fall on Kharkiv and nearby towns. The new direction on the use of the U.S. weapons will allow Ukraine to employ American weapons to intercept Russian missiles that are targeting Kharkiv, and to attack concentrations of Russian troops just over the border in the vicinity of the city. This will allow for Ukraine to aim for high value targets such as command and control centers, artillery, logistics and air defence units that are located on Russian territory near Kharkiv and concentrating or rehearsing future operations against Ukraine. Russian propagandists must be devastated. No instruction manuals have been received from the AP (administration of the president) as yet, so they are keeping num about it.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Where is Putin’s bunker located?
Answer: Vladimir Putin has multiple bunkers — on this photo, his residence in Altai (which went on fire yesterday), where one of such bunkers is located. Reportedly, Putin’s Altai nuclear bunker is built in the side of a mountain in Ongudai district and is supposed to be able to hold thousands of people. The nearby residence is officially registered as Gazprom sanatorium, but guarded by the presidential security guards. Vladimir Putin brought the Italian Prime Minister Berlusconi here in 2015. The construction of the residence cost 3 billion ruble (USD $136 million in 2009 money). The cost of the bunker will be many times higher. In 2011, “Autoreview” journalists, as part of a joint investigation with “Novaya Gazeta”, tried to get into the sanatorium, but the security turned them away, citing the special status of the facility intended for the country's top officials. Ongudai district in Altai region is located near the Russian border with Kazakhstan, China and Mongolia. Putin stayed at this “sanatorium” many times during unofficial visits to the Altai Mountains, so it’s safe to say, no one else would be allowed to “recuperate” there, knowing the level of paranoia of the Kremlin usurper. Presumably, every Putin’s residence has a bunker big enough to accommodate a team of hundreds, if not thousands. It’s believed that Putin has about 20 residences in Russia built for his exclusive use. A recent leak of the map showing top secret locations that the ministry of defence contractors connected to high-speed internet by fiber-optic cable might be showing all of them. And this means, Putin is probably already busy building new bunkers, hoping to outsmart Americans and find a safe place to hide where he wouldn’t be found.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What do you think of Russian Finance Ministry's projection of a budget deficit of 0.8% of Russia’s GDP for 2024?
Answer: The Russian federal budget deficit for January - April of this year amounted to 3.963 trillion ruble (USD $39 billion), the Federal Treasury of the Russian Federation reported. In early May 2024, Russia’s Ministry of Finance said there would be a deficit of 1.5 trillion ruble ($15 billion) — that’s 260% of the predicted figure. The whole annual budget deficit was supposed to be only 1.6 trillion rub. ($16 billion). Only the deficit of January-April 2024 makes 1.8% of Russia’s GDP. So, they are running short of money for sure. The only way to compensate for that is to get much higher income during the remaining months of the year. What can be expected next: That’s why Putin really needs to freeze the war in Ukraine. The Russian economy is working in the crisis mode for 2.5 years. Things start going wrong right, left and centre. Any major issue can become the proverbial “last straw”.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: What impact could imprisoned ultranationalist Igor Girkin's political maneuvers have on Russian President Vladimir Putin?
Answer: Yesterday, the appeal court upheld the verdict of the Moscow City Court against the 53-year-old former commander of pro-Russian separatists in Donetsk Igor Girkin. Girkin (Strelkov), who is a former FSB officer, was arrested a month after the infamous Prigozhin’s coup of June 2023, and charged with “extremism”. While we know there is basically no such thing as “a former FSB officer” (you are always either an asset of the force — or a traitor, sentenced to elimination), for a long time, Girkin’s rants about the sorry state of affairs in the Russian army fighting in Ukraine didn’t cause him any trouble. So much so that most people decided that Girkin-Strelkov had powerful backers among the FSB ranks who were playing their own game. But after Prigozhin’s aborted coup, the rules of the game obviously changed. As soon as Prigozhin and his goons had been removed from the scene and their influence nullified, Girkin (who was actually a fierce opponent of Prigozhin) was arrested and thrown in Lefortovo prison — the same FSB pre-trial jail where recently arrested generals of the ministry of defence are now locked up. In January 2024, Girkin was found guilty and sentenced to 4 years in prison. Girkin’s family members were not allowed into the court during yesterday’s hearing, his wife Miroslava Reginskaya wrote on Telegram. In the near future, Girkin will be transferred to the penal colony. It was previously reported that the ex-separatist leader expressed a desire to join the Russian armed forces and go to the war in Ukraine — the war, which he personally unleashed in 2014. Under the Russian law, those convicted of extremism are not eligible for “conditional release” granted to those who sign the contract with the ministry of defence, to go to the war. Thus, Girkin can only sign an army contract if Vladimir Putin pardons him. Which will never happen — free and unhinged Girkin is a real threat to Putin’s regime, especially with a weapon in his hands. Plus he knows too much and would be a perfect witness for Putin’s Hague trial. And his worst offense, he insulted Putin personally — which makes Girkin a “traitor”, an unforgivable sin in the eyes of vengeful Putin. When his time of release gets near, Girkin will either “suddenly die” or get a new jail term — this time a much longer one. Girkin posted enough to be sentenced for “treason”, “discrediting the army” — or dozens of other offenses, designed by Putin’s regime to lock up the people who cause trouble. Girkin is finished. Anyone who is still supporting him might find themselves in FSB “interview rooms” pretty soon.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Are Russians now scared that Ukrainians can bomb civilians in Moscow and Russia as well?
Answer: While Ukrainians have no habit to bomb civilians (unlike the Russian troops, who are targeting civilians purposefully and deliberately), the Russian media is already hysterical that Ukrainians can now hit military targets with western-made weapons. So much so that Symonyan’s propaganda outlet “Russia Today” published the map above, trying to scare Russian citizens — I suppose, to inspire them into signing up for the war in Ukraine. Margarita (may Lord show justice to her lost soul) has never been particularly bright, but she’s usually more intuitive than this — so my take is, the instructions came directly from the administration of the president, which has been making heaps of haphazard decisions lately. The infographic demonstrated how far Ukraine can strike if the West lifts restrictions on the use of weapons supplied to the Ukrainian Armed Forces — trying to mentally prepare Russians for the fact that restrictions will soon be lifted. This comes as Muscovites are being grabbed on city streets and sent to military regiments, despite chronic illnesses and deferments from military service, issued by their workplaces. There are 500,000 Russian troops already in Ukraine and Putin wants to double the size of his occupational army. For that sacred goal, all means are justified. Meanwhile, already 12 countries allowed Ukraine to use their weapons to strike military targets on the territory of Russia: The pressure intensifies on Germany and the USA to follow the suit. There are already ambiguous statements being made by the U.S. Secretary of State Blinken and German chancellor Scholz about Ukraine being able “to make its own decisions” and having the right to use German weapons within “the frame of international laws” against the Russian aggression. It’s clear where the vector of the next moves by the USA and Germany points. That’s what Putin has to deal with on the 826th day of the special military operation to “take Kyiv in 3 days”.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is Russia as strong as people like to think? It seems that Russia is a country with a poor economy, not many diplomatic ties, an aging arsenal, and a population equal to a third of the USA's. Do people overestimate Russia?
Answer: The poor state of Russia’s economy is evident — the government is urgently raising taxes, because there’s no money to finance the war in Ukraine. Ordinary Russians will finance the war they supported — or chose not to object. Russia’s government allocated the highest ever money to defence in its 2024 budget, obviously hoping to end the war this year — the state budget for 2025 pre-planned much less money for the army. If Putin wants to continue the war in 2025, he needs to find some money for it — and fast. (On the photo — the man identifying as Vladimir Putin at the press-conference in Tashkent on May 28, 2024.) The continuous aid by the USA and European Union destroyed Kremlin’s plans, and now Putin urgently needs to find money to buy components to continue building missiles and munitions in the quantities required to maintain the pressure on the Ukrainian defence forces and not lose more territories — it was bad enough to lose half of the captured territories in 2022 to the failed siege of Kyiv and swift Ukrainian counteroffensives in Kharkiv and Kherson regions. By 11 November 2022, Ukrainian forces had liberated the area of 74,443 km2 (28,743 sq mi) from Russian occupation (that’s more than the size of Ireland), leaving Russia with control of about 18% of Ukraine's territory. Russia’s touted “devastating offensive in the Kharkiv region” (the plan was to besiege the city and take it without destroying the buildings and infrastructure) completely stalled within days from its start on May 10, 2024. Russia isn’t strong enough to concentrate troops in one sector, to make substantial and sustainable gains. Reportedly, Russians also use much less heavy equipment in this last offensive, suggesting that their stocks are running out. The overspending on the war led Russia to substantial budget deficits, which it has to address now, as it’s obvious that Ukraine will continue to get aid from the USA. Russia's loss of profitable energy sales to Europe and heightened military expenditures compelled the country to tap into its sovereign wealth fund and seek loans from state-owned banks to address the budget deficits over the past 2 years. The proposed tax hike aims to generate $29 billion annually, Finance Minister Anton Siluanov stated. The high hopes may not become a reality. This development is of historic proportions: for a long time, Russia bragged about offering “one of the most favorable tax regimes in the world”, with the flat rate of 13% income tax for individuals. Now, this will be gone — gone forever. The only way is up. The changes are announced as new higher-tax thresholds for “top earners” (everyone who earns over 2,000 Euro per month). The corporation tax is also lifted: from 20% to 25%. Only the companies involved in military production for the needs of the state might be given tax breaks. This is why economist Belousov was appointed as the minister of defence, and that’s why Russia is now starting the creeping tax hikes. But Russia’s economic problems aren’t limited by defence spending. The agriculture and farming this year suffered terrible losses: first, grain fields had been washed off by abnormal floods, and then future crops of vegetables, fruit and berries had been destroyed by abnormal frosts in several regions. That’s the picture of snow-covered Tomsk last night. They were getting ready to open the beach season. In the central regions of Russia, abnormal frosts hit earlier this month. The situation is so dire that the Russian ministry of agriculture wants to announce a state of emergency of federal significance due to the May frosts, which destroyed crops in the key food producing regions of the country. The frosts affected crops in 23 Russia’s regions: 18 million tons of grain harvest had been lost. This means, Russia will only be able to produce 129 million tons of grains, instead of 142–147 million tons, as was forecasted. “In total, 1.5 million hectares of cultivated areas were affected,” the head of grain producers union Arkady Zlochevsky said at a press conference on Monday, pointing that Russia hadn’t had such late frosts for over 100 years. Not more than 60% could potentially be re-sown — but even if the farmers tried to do it, the potential harvest would be conditional on long summer, with the real possibility that the grains will end up under the snow. As a result, a series of bankruptcies of agricultural producers is expected, who have already been hit by the recent increase in export duties, and then the redistribution of land. “The crisis management” of the Russian economy began a while ago — the upcoming tax hikes are just another step on that slippery slope. Meanwhile, the inflation in Russia is speeding up. The Central Bank is expected to raise its base rate any day — the question is by how much. And if you didn’t know, the base interest rate in Russia is already whopping 16%. Putin’s propagandists can say all they want about “the great state of the Russian economy despite the war and sanctions”, but both the government and the population can clearly see what is about to unfold.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is Russia Today a trustworthy news source?
Answer: “Russia Today” has been banned in the European Union and Canada for spreading Kremlin disinformation. Independent service providers in over 10 countries also suspended broadcasts of RT. Social media websites (except X) followed by blocking external links to RT's website and restricting access to RT's content. In the UK, “Russia Today” was banned in September 2015: Ofcom found RT in breach of the impartiality rules in its coverage of events in Ukraine and Syria. “Russia rebukes Biden claim that U.S. won WWII,” RT posted today on X. The rest of the world thinks otherwise. Russia isn’t even on the list — but the U.S. is. I know: Russia was part of the Soviet Union, which won WWII. So was Ukraine. So was Kazakhstan. So was Armenia. So was Georgia. So were — technically — Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. There were 15 republics in the Soviet Union, which all are now independent countries. None of these countries, though, claims that it single-handedly “saved the world from fascism”. Russia does. And its propaganda-permeated population repeats after the Russian state media — which includes “Russia Today”. The Kremlin regime transformed state-controlled media into instruments of information manipulation and information warfare. “Russia Today” is definitely not a trustworthy news source. It’s a Kremlin’s weapon.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: How much support does Vladimir Putin have for the invasion of Ukraine among his own people?
Answer: This Russian soldier who lost his limb in Ukraine complains that he didn’t receive the payments of 3 million rub. (USD $30,000) for the heavy injury and 812,000 rub. ($8,120) for disability, which were promised by recruiters. He says that “the other guys” who served with him didn’t get payments either. His last hope to get paid what they were promised was to record a video appeal to Vladimir Putin — in his video, he repeats Putin’s name more than once, saying that all his former written requests addressed to Putin had been forwarded to the ministry of defence, but he got no answers from them. (Video in the comments below.) There are literally thousands injured soldiers like him — only in 2023, over 140,000 more applications were filed in Russia with requests for wheelchairs and prosthetics. In Moscow, police has been raiding streets since Putin’s “inauguration”, grabbing young men and taking them to military recruitment offices. The men are put through the commission of medics, found “fit for military service” (despite many of them having chronic health conditions included on the list of diseases with which people shouldn’t be drafted), and sent to military units. Those who already had documents with the military where it’s recorded that they are ill, are still detained and not allowed to leave. The men are told they would have to serve in the army anyway, and they better sign that they agree to do it. At a the military office on Ugreshskaya Street, several dozen conscripts who are unfit or partially fit for service are being forcibly detained. Their family members came to the place and recorded video messages demanding the release of the men. Looks like while the Russian media promotes “overwhelming support” for Putin’s invasion, not many Russians are willing to allow their family members anywhere near the army. And those who survived the meat grinder of the Ukrainian front aren’t having much support — not even now, while Putin still needs great PR for the war in Ukraine. Imagine what’s going to happen when the war is over and those who lost their health there become an annoying reminder of the biggest blunder in the recent history of Russia. If you remember, Stalin loaded maimed WWII veterans in paddy wagons and shipped them to remote islands and locations that they couldn’t leave — so that the streets of the Soviet cities weren’t disturbed by the unsightly invalids, forced to beg to survive. That’s where these invalids died. They were sent there to die. And that was the war that the Soviets bragged they have “won”.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why did the USSR attack Finland in 1939?
Answer: in 1939, the USSR propaganda was saying the same things about Finland that it’s saying about Ukraine today, to justify the attack: Soviets proclaimed that a “junta under the control of overseas masters” was in power in Finland — and the Soviets weren’t invaders, but “liberators.” The Soviet communists loathed seeing how happily the former part of the Russian Empire could live without Russia, and they decided to destroy this country, bomb it from planes and crush it with tanks. Finland before the war with the Soviets. For a long time, regiments of the Red Army were concentrating around the border with Finland, engaging in all types of vile provocations. At the same time, the Kremlin was blaming “the Finnish military under the leadership of the White Finnish butcher Mannerheim and his overseas masters” for altercations. Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim (1867–1951) charted the course of Finnish history and was voted greatest Finn of all time. He served in the Russian Imperial Army for decades, and later became a war hero in his home country of Finland. He was the symbol of the Finnish struggle against Soviet Russia during the Winter War of 1939–1940. The Soviet plan to take over Finland was touted as “help to the brotherly Finnish nation”. For that, the fictitious “People's Republic of Finland” was created in the Kremlin, as opposition to the “Helsinki Junta”. That “brotherly help” was to send Soviet tanks all the way to Helsinki — naturally, to “liberate long-suffering Finnish people” from the horrible regime that was oppressing them. Apparently, the Soviet propagandists believed that the Finnish people loathed their government just as much as the Soviet people loathed theirs, that’s why they prepared such propaganda. In reality, Finns rose up not against the “White Finnish junta”, but against the Soviet invaders. In the very first days of the war, the Soviets began bombing Helsinki — the Red Army pilots were doing it during the day, at lunchtime, when there were many people in the streets. The photo shows destruction from Soviet bombs on Frederiksgatan Street. Later, when footage of burning Helsinki spread all over the world, the Soviets began to lie that they bombed “only military targets,” but in fact, most of the bombs fell in the city center — around the central train station and major streets. Stalin's tactics of “not a step back” with barrier troops behind the storm regiments were first used in the Finnish war (the task of “barrier troops” was to shoot anyone trying to retreat). The photo shows Red Army soldiers frozen in a trench: the soldiers were simply left to freeze in the forest. Red Army soldiers captured by Finns. Contrary to the Soviet propaganda, the Finns treated Soviet prisoners better than their own state: Finns gave the captives hot food and kept them warm. In the USSR, all these imprisoned by the enemy were sent to GULAG for 10 years, on their return. The Finns fought heroically for their country. One of the notable operations was the battle on the Raat road, in which the Finns defeated the 44th division of the Soviets. The soldiers of the 44th Division scattered through the forest: most of the 17,000 personnel lost in the operation weren’t killed by Finnish bullets, but simply froze to death. A considerable part of the dead soldiers were Ukrainians and Belarusians, whom the Soviets mobilized to fight against Finns — although the Finns did nothing wrong to Ukrainians and Belarusians. The Soviets lost so many soldiers and machinery that they couldn’t continue the war. The Red Army wasn't able to crush the Finnish resistance as planned. Stalin asked for negotiations and signed a “peace deal” with the Finns. Britain and France had considered providing the Finns with military assistance, but they took too long to actually deliver any. Still, one of the reasons why Stalin offered the peace deal to Finland was his worry to be faced with a war against France and Britain. Stalin planned to use the 1940 Peace Treaty (which emasculated Finnish defensive lines) as an interim break, followed by a renewed attack — once the threat of the Western intervention was over. The cost to Finland was the loss of 11% of its territory — in fact, Stalin demanded more land than the Red Army managed to occupy. 410,000 Finns living on the territories that were being transferred to the USSR (12% of the population of Finland at the time) had to leave their houses and evacuate to the regions that Finland managed to save, because they didn’t wish to live under the Soviet rule. Almost the whole population of the ceded territories chose to relocate. Stalin didn’t object the people leaving, but demanded that the buildings and machinery were left behind intact. The war lasted 105 days — 3.5 months. The “peace deal” was signed in March 1940. In just 3 months, in June 1940, Stalin invaded and annexed 3 Baltic countries — Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. For the next 50 years, the Baltics had to live under the Soviet occupation, undergo extensive Russification, had to send their men to the Soviet army — including during the period of the USSR invasion of Afghanistan. Meanwhile, the Finns had built one of the richest and happiest countries on Earth.

Question: Whatever happened to Mathias Rust the German man who landed a plane in Moscow during the 1980s?
Answer: 37 years ago, on May 28, 1987, German man Matthias Rust's plane landed on the Red Square in Moscow. 19-year-old German teenager initially intended to land in the Kremlin, but he decided that landing inside, hidden by the Kremlin walls, would have allowed the KGB to arrest him and deny the incident. This is why he changed his landing place to the Red Square. Rust flew his Reims Cessna 172P from Helsinki, Finland, which was the last stop of his long trip. He designed the trip purposefully, to avoid flying over the East Germany’s air space. Instead of returning to Hamburg, as authorized, he flew to Moscow. On the approach to Moscow, there was a major concentration of fighter bases and the air space was very busy. Radars and surface to air missile sites were supposed to be on alert against any enemy threats. Rust evaded it all by flying his Cessna at roof-top height, and managed to land on stone-paved Red Square, near the famous cathedral. His passing so deep into the heart of the USSR and landing in the most iconic square of Moscow, caused an immense humiliation to the Soviet War Machine — although the KGB tried to play it down. Rust managed to show just how rusty the Soviet defence really was. In fact, the whole Soviet Union was rusty. Rust was prosecuted in the USSR for entering the Soviet air space without authorization and “malicious hooligansim”, and sentenced to 4 years in a labor camp — of which he only served 14 months. In August 1988, Rust was pardoned and released, and he returned to Germany. This was in the middle of Perestroika, announced by Mikhail Gorbachev in April 1987 — weeks before Rust’s scandalous arrival. Then things went wrong for Rust, until they got better. Within a year of returning to Hamburg, he stabbed a colleague at a hospital where he worked (a female nurse who refused his advances), and ended up for 15 months behind bars again. Blame the Russian prisons for his disturbed mental state. When freed, he became a financial analyst and a yoga instructor. Reportedly, he also played high stakes poker, which he used as an income stream. Mathias Rust in 2012. He doesn’t give comments to media anymore. Rust stated he had no regrets about what he did. He was happy that he was able to help President Gorbachev to initiate his reforms. Rust's flight through the extensive Soviet air defence system — presumed impenetrable — indeed helped Mikhail Gorbachev in the implementation of his reforms. Gorbachev was able to dismiss numerous military officials opposed to his policies. Among them, the Minister of Defence Sergei Sokolov and the Commander-in-Chief of the Air Defence Forces Alexander Koldunov were fired. Over the next few months more than 150 people lost their jobs. Soviets returned Rust’s Cessna to his flying club. It changed hands a few times, until it finally found its place in the Deutsches Technikmuseum in Berlin, as a symbol of one audacious pilot’s attempt to improve relations between East and West.

Question: How much does a teacher earn in Russia?
Answer: How much teachers earn in Russia depends on the city. In Moscow, wages are 2.5 times higher than in regional towns. According to the latest data, the base monthly salary of a school teacher in the Kostroma region is 19,200 ruble (USD $192). Each teacher on average works for 1.65 people (not the regular 40 hours per week but 99 hours per week). That’s both because of the lack of personnel and low pay — unless you pick extra hours, you’d struggle to survive. At the end, the average monthly paycheck of a teacher in Kostroma region comes to 36,200 rub. ($362). In other words, the typical base salary of a teacher in the regions of Central Russia is 20-25 thousand ruble per month. Accordingly, working at 1.5 the rate allows you to increase your income to the level of a salesperson-cashier at a local store. Young teachers without experience earn even less. Great life that Putin created for Russian educators.
